title: Notations
body_md:
We write \(\operatorname{Law}(X)\) for the law of a random variable \(X\).
For probability densities \(
u\) and \(\pi\), write the total variation distance as
\(\operatorname{TV}(
u,\pi):=\sup_A\lvert
u(A)-\pi(A)vert\).  When \(
u\ll\pi\), the
order-\(r\) R'enyi divergence for \(r>1\) is
\(D_r(
u\Vert\pi):= rac{1}{r-1}\log\int
( rac{
u(x)}{\pi(x)})^r\pi(x)\,\mathrm{d} x\).  In
particular, the $\chi^2$ divergence is
\(\chi^2(
u\Vert\pi):=\int( rac{
u(x)}{\pi(x)}-1)^2\pi(x)\,\mathrm{d} x
=\mathrm{e}^{D_2(
u\Vert\pi)}-1\), and
\(\operatorname{TV}(
u,\pi)\le	frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(
u\Vert\pi)}\).  We call \(
u\)
a constant-\(D_2\) warm start of \(\pi\) if
\(D_2(
u\Vert\pi)=O(1)\). The notations \(\widetilde O(\cdot), \widetilde\Theta(\cdot)\) suppress polylogarithmic factors in the displayed problem parameters. 
\([a]_+:=\max\{a,0\}\).

label: ass:target
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:target}
We assume that the target density is
\(\pi(x)\propto\mathrm{e}^{-V(x)}\), where the potential
\(V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is \(\alpha\)-strongly convex and \(\beta\)-smooth,
i.e., \(\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\lVertx-x'\rVert^2\le
V(x)-V(x')-\langle\nabla V(x'),x-x'\rangle\le
\tfrac{\beta}{2}\lVertx-x'\rVert^2\) for all \(x,x'\in\mathbb R^d\).  We denote the condition
number by \(\kappa:=\beta/\alpha\).

head: environment
name: Exactness of the framework

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\varphi_\eta:=\mathcal N(0,\eta I_d)\), so that \(\Pi_\eta(x,y)=\pi(x)\varphi_\eta(y-x)\).  For every \(f\),
\begin{align*}
    \mathop{\textstyle\int} f(x,2x-y)\,\pi(x)\varphi_\eta(y-x)\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y
    =\mathop{\textstyle\int} f(x,y')\,\pi(x)\varphi_\eta(x-y')\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y'
    =\mathop{\textstyle\int} f\,\mathrm{d}\Pi_\eta.
\end{align*}
Hence the reflection preserves \(\Pi_\eta\).  Now fix \(y\) and let
\(\overline M_y(x,x')=(1-\rho)M_y(x,x')+\rho q_y(x')\) be the mixture distribution of the accelerated and RGO branches.  Since \(M_y\) preserves \(q_y\),
\begin{align*}
  \mathop{\textstyle\int} q_y(x)M_y(x,x')\,\mathrm{d} x = q_y(x')
  \implies
  \mathop{\textstyle\int}[\mathop{\textstyle\int} f(x',y)\overline M_y(x,x')\,\mathrm{d} x']q_y(x)\,\mathrm{d} x
 =\mathop{\textstyle\int} f(x',y)q_y(x')\,\mathrm{d} x'.
\end{align*}
Thus the second update preserves the conditional law \(q_y\) for every \(y\).  Composing it with the reflection preserves \(\Pi_\eta\), whose position marginal is \(\pi\).

body_md:
\label{prop:flux-main-reversal}
Suppose \(\beta\eta\le1/2\).
 
 
 
Conditional on the reflected auxiliary value
\(Y_{k+1}=y\), if the input position satisfies \(X_k\mid Y_{k+1}=y\sim q_y\), then the output satisfies \(X_{k+1}\mid Y_{k+1}=y\sim q_y\)  as well.

label: thm:persistent-finite
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:persistent-finite}
Under \cref{ass:target}, let \(\nu_0\) satisfy
\(D_2(\nu_0\Vert\pi)\le\Delta\), and let
\(\varepsilon\le1/2\).  There exist fixed universal constants \(c,C>0\) so that the following holds.
Define
\(\Lambda_\varepsilon=\Delta+\log(Cd\kappa/\varepsilon)\) and
\(\eta=c/\{\beta(\sqrt{d\Lambda_\varepsilon}+\Lambda_\varepsilon)\}\).
Initialize \(X_0\sim\nu_0\),
\(Y_0\mid X_0\sim\mathcal N(X_0,\eta I_d)\), and independently \(P_0\sim\gamma_d\).  Run the implementable algorithm specified in
\cref{persistent:sec:implementation}; its output law \(\widehat\nu\) satisfies
\(\operatorname{TV}(\widehat\nu,\pi)\le\varepsilon\).  If
\(N_{\mathrm{qry}}\) counts all oracle queries and \(N_{\mathrm{rgo}}\)
counts approximate-RGO calls, then
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E N_{\mathrm{qry}}
 &\le\widetilde O(
 \sqrt\kappa\,(\Delta+\log(8/\varepsilon))
 (\sqrt{d\Lambda_\varepsilon}+\Lambda_\varepsilon)^{1/2}),
 \label{eq:persistent-general-complexity}\\
 \mathbb E N_{\mathrm{rgo}}
 &\le\widetilde O(\Delta+\log(8/\varepsilon)).
 \nonumber
\end{align}
In particular, a constant-\(D_2\) warm start gives
\(\widetilde O(\sqrt\kappa d^{1/4})\) expected oracle queries and only
\(\operatorname{polylog}(d,\kappa,1/\varepsilon)\) expected RGO calls.

label: flux:lem:conditional-geometry
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{flux:lem:conditional-geometry}
For every \(y\),
\[
 \frac1{1+s}I\preceq\Sigma_y\preceq\frac1{1+a}I,
 \qquad
 \frac a{1+a}I\preceq I-\Sigma_y\preceq\frac s{1+s}I.
\]
If \(\Pi_\eta^Y(y)\propto \mathrm{e}^{-U_\eta(y)}\), then
\[
 \nabla U_\eta(y)=\eta^{-1}\{y-\mathbb E[X\mid Y=y]\},\qquad
 \nabla^2U_\eta(y)=\eta^{-1}(I-\Sigma_y),
\]
and hence
\(\alpha(1+a)^{-1}I\preceq\nabla^2U_\eta
\preceq\beta(1+s)^{-1}I\).
Moreover, when \(s<1\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E g_y(W)=-\bar w_y,\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(W,g_y(W))=I-\Sigma_y,\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(g_y(W))\preceq\frac{s}{1-s}(I-\Sigma_y).
 \label{flux:eq:conditional-identities}
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Localized conditional geometry

title: Proof
body_md:
The normalized conditional potential has curvature between
\((1+a)I\) and \((1+s)I\).  Brascamp--Lieb gives the upper covariance
bound.  The information inequality gives
\(\operatorname{Cov}(W)\succeq\{\mathbb E\nabla^2[-\log q_y^w(W)]\}^{-1}
\succeq(1+s)^{-1}I\), proving the remaining covariance bounds.
Differentiating the conditional normalizer gives the two identities for
\(U_\eta\).

For \cref{flux:eq:conditional-identities}, use
\(\nabla\log q_y^w(w)=-w-g_y(w)\).  Integration by parts first gives
\(\mathbb E(W+g_y(W))=0\) and
\(\Sigma_y+\operatorname{Cov}(W,g_y(W))=I\).  Applying it once more to \(g_y\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E\nabla g_y(W)=I-\Sigma_y+\operatorname{Cov}(g_y(W)).
\]
The conditional law has Poincar\'e constant at most one, while
\(0\preceq\nabla g_y\preceq sI\).  Therefore
\(\operatorname{Cov}(g_y(W))\preceq s\mathbb E\nabla g_y(W)\); rearrangement proves the last
claim.  These standard Brascamp--Lieb and integration-by-parts facts are
reviewed, for example, by \citet{chewi2023log}.  The extension from smooth
potentials and test functions to the regularity in \cref{ass:target} is
collected in \cref{flux:app:regularity}.

label: flux:prop:fixed-validity
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{flux:prop:fixed-validity}
For every fixed \((y,\widetilde w)\), the preceding process is
non-explosive and preserves \(q_y^w\otimes\gamma_d\).  If
\(\mathsf S_t^{y,\widetilde w}\) is its transition operator and
\((Jf)(w,p)=f(w,-p)\), then
\[
 (\mathsf S_t^{y,\widetilde w})^*=J\mathsf S_t^{y,\widetilde w}J.
\]
It is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup on
\(L^2(q_y^w\otimes\gamma_d)\).
Consequently, inserting an independent Gaussian momentum, running for a
fixed time, and discarding momentum gives a reversible position kernel for
\(q_y^w\).  The conclusion remains true after averaging over any reference
law independent of the incoming \((W,P)\) conditional on \(Y=y\).
head: environment
name: Fixed-reference validity

title: Proof
body_md:
The calculation follows the usual skew-balance argument for event-driven
kinetic samplers
\citep{vanetti2017piecewise,bierkens2020boomerang,michel2020forward,
monmarche2022exact}; we give the semigroup step because our reference
motion also contains Langevin noise.

The proof has three steps.  First, a trajectory with no event can be
reversed after flipping momentum; its no-event probability supplies exactly
the likelihood correction caused by the residual force.  Second, the
Rayleigh update balances the stationary probability flow through a single
collision.  Finally, we sum these identities over the number and times of
the collisions.  This proves reversal of the complete process as well as
invariance.

\emph{Non-explosion.}
With
\(\mathcal V=1+\{\lVertw+b_{\rm ref}\rVert^2+\lVertp\rVert^2\}/2\), the full
generator obeys
\(\mathcal L\mathcal V\le C_{\widetilde w}(1+\mathcal V)\), and the event
rate is at most \(C_{\widetilde w}(1+\mathcal V)\), where
\(C_{\widetilde w}\) is a finite constant that may depend on the fixed
reference.  Indeed, a jump changes \(\mathcal V\) by
\((R^2-z^2)/2\), \(\mathbb E R^2=2\), and
\(\lVerth(w)\rVert\le s\lVertw-\widetilde w\rVert\).
A stopped Dynkin formula and Gronwall bound both
\(\mathbb E\mathcal V(W_t,P_t)\) and the
expected event count on every finite interval.  The recursive
integrated-hazard construction is therefore well defined and
non-explosive.

\emph{Reversal between and at events.}
Let \(Z_t^0=(W_t^0,P_t^0)\) be the affine Langevin diffusion without
events, let \(\lambda(w,p)=[p^\mathrm{T} h(w)]_+\), and define its killed
semigroup---that is, its transition weighted by the probability of seeing
no event---by
\[
 \mathsf D_tf(z)=\mathbb E_z\!\left[
 \mathrm{e}^{-\int_0^t\lambda(Z_u^0)\,\mathrm{d} u}f(Z_t^0)\right].
\]
The affine diffusion is invariant and momentum-reversible for the Gaussian
density
\(\mu_{\rm ref}\propto
\exp\{-\lVertw+b_{\rm ref}\rVert^2/2-\lVertp\rVert^2/2\}\).
For the desired density \(\mu=q_y^w\otimes\gamma_d\), the ratio
\(\varrho=\mathrm{d}\mu/\mathrm{d}\mu_{\rm ref}\) satisfies
\(\nabla\log\varrho=-h\).  Since the position
path is absolutely continuous,
\[
 \frac{\varrho(W_t^0)}{\varrho(W_0^0)}
 =\exp\left\{-\int_0^tP_u^{0\mathrm{T}}h(W_u^0)\,\mathrm{d} u\right\}
 =\exp\left\{-\int_0^t(\lambda-\lambda\circ J)(Z_u^0)\,\mathrm{d} u\right\}.
\]
Stationary path reversal for the affine diffusion therefore gives
\(\mathsf D_t^*=J\mathsf D_tJ\) first for bounded nonnegative functions.
Taking one test function equal to one shows \(\mu\mathsf D_t\le\mu\), and Jensen's inequality
extends the identity to \(L^2(\mu)\).

Let \(\mathcal G\) be the gain kernel: it applies one collision, weighted by
the rate at which that collision occurs.  At fixed \(w\), write the incoming momentum as
\(p=v+zn\), where \(v\perp n\) and \(z>0\).  Apart from a common constant,
the stationary marked flux is
\[
 q_y^w(w)\lVerth(w)\rVert\varphi_{d-1}(v)
 z \mathrm{e}^{-z^2/2}r \mathrm{e}^{-r^2/2}\,
 \mathrm{d} w\,\mathrm{d} v\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} r,\qquad z,r>0.
\]
Here \(\varphi_{d-1}\) is the standard Gaussian density on the subspace
orthogonal to \(n\).
It is unchanged by \((v,z,r)\mapsto(-v,r,z)\), which turns a marked
transition into the momentum reversal of its time-reversed transition.
Thus \(\mathcal G^*=J\mathcal GJ\) in the corresponding kernel sense.

The contribution of paths with exactly \(m\) events is the time-simplex
integral of
\(\mathsf D_{t_0}\mathcal G\mathsf D_{t_1}\cdots
\mathcal G\mathsf D_{t_m}\).
Reversing the simplex coordinates and using the preceding two identities
shows that its adjoint is obtained by conjugating with \(J\).  Tonelli
justifies this calculation for nonnegative tests, and non-explosion makes
the sum over \(m\) conservative, meaning that it retains total probability
one.  Summing proves
\((\mathsf S_t^{y,\widetilde w})^*=J\mathsf S_t^{y,\widetilde w}J\);
taking one test
function equal to one proves invariance.  Jensen gives \(L^2\)
contractivity, while stochastic continuity and density of bounded
continuous compactly supported functions give strong continuity.

Finally, if \(\iota f(w,p)=f(w)\) and
\(\mathsf M u(w)=\int u(w,p)\,\gamma_d(\mathrm{d} p)\), then
\(\mathsf M=\iota^*\), \(J\iota=\iota\), and \(\mathsf M J=\mathsf M\).
Thus inserting a Gaussian momentum and then discarding it are adjoint
operations.  Suppressing the fixed superscripts \((y,\widetilde w)\),
\((\mathsf M\mathsf S_t\iota)^*=\mathsf M\mathsf S_t\iota\).
Conditioning on an
independent reference and applying Fubini proves the last assertion.

label: flux:lem:affine-evolution
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{flux:lem:affine-evolution}
The two observables belong to the \(L^2(q_y^w\otimes\gamma_d)\) generator
domain and satisfy
\[
 \mathcal L\ell_{u,y}=m_u,\qquad
 \mathcal Lm_u=-\ell_{u,y}-\gamma m_u+k_{u,\widetilde w}.
\]
Writing \(\omega=\sqrt{1-\gamma^2/4}\), set
\[
 A_\gamma(t)=\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma t/2}
 \left\{\cos(\omega t)+\frac\gamma{2\omega}\sin(\omega t)\right\},
 \qquad
 B_\gamma(t)=\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma t/2}\frac{\sin(\omega t)}\omega.
\]
Then, for the fixed-reference semigroup,
\[
 \mathsf S_t^{y,\widetilde w}\ell_{u,y}
 =A_\gamma(t)\ell_{u,y}+B_\gamma(t)m_u
  +\int_0^tB_\gamma(t-r)
       \mathsf S_r^{y,\widetilde w}k_{u,\widetilde w}\,\mathrm{d} r.
\]
At \(T_\gamma=\pi/\omega\), this becomes
\begin{equation}
 (I+\mathsf S_{T_\gamma}^{y,\widetilde w})\ell_{u,y}
 =(1-\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma T_\gamma/2})\ell_{u,y}
  +\int_0^{T_\gamma}B_\gamma(T_\gamma-r)
       \mathsf S_r^{y,\widetilde w}k_{u,\widetilde w}\,\mathrm{d} r.
 \label{flux:eq:halfturn-duhamel}
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Affine evolution

title: Proof
body_md:
The deterministic part of the generator gives
\(\mathcal L\ell_{u,y}=m_u\) and
\(-\ell_{u,y}-\gamma m_u-u^\mathrm{T}(\bar w_y+b_{\rm ref})\) in the momentum
coordinate.
At an event, the momentum change is
\(-(Z+R)u^\mathrm{T} n\), where \(Z=p^\mathrm{T} n>0\); multiplying its conditional
mean by the rate \(\lVerth\rVert Z\) gives the remaining term
\(-u^\mathrm{T} h\,\psi(Z)\).

These quantities are square integrable because \(q_y^w\) has Gaussian
tails, \(h\) grows at most linearly, and \(p^\mathrm{T} n\) is standard normal
conditional on the position.  Applying the stopped Dynkin formula and then
removing the stopping time using the Lyapunov bound in
\cref{flux:prop:fixed-validity} gives, after suppressing the fixed
superscripts \((y,\widetilde w)\),
\[
 \mathsf S_t\ell_{u,y}-\ell_{u,y}
 =\int_0^t\mathsf S_rm_u\,\mathrm{d} r,\qquad
 \mathsf S_tm_u-m_u
 =\int_0^t\mathsf S_r(-\ell_{u,y}-\gamma m_u
                       +k_{u,\widetilde w})\,\mathrm{d} r.
\]
Strong continuity and division by \(t\) prove the generator-domain
statements.  Solving the resulting two-dimensional linear equation by
variation of constants gives the displayed formula.  At \(T_\gamma\),
\(B_\gamma(T_\gamma)=0\) and
\(A_\gamma(T_\gamma)=-\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma T_\gamma/2}\), which proves
\cref{flux:eq:halfturn-duhamel}.
head: environment

label: flux:eq:forcing-moment
title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(W,\widetilde W\) be independent with law \(q_y^w\), and average
first over the Gaussian momentum; we denote this last expectation by
\(\mathbb E_{P}\).  Direct one-dimensional Gaussian
integration gives
\(\mathbb E\psi(Z)=1\) and
\(\operatorname{Var}\psi(Z)=5/2+\pi/4\) for \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\).  Using
\(\mathbb E g_y(W)=-\bar w_y\), we obtain
\[
 \mathbb E_P k_{u,\widetilde W}
 =-u^\mathrm{T}\{g_y(W)-\mathbb E g_y(W)\},
\]
while the conditional momentum variance is
\((5/2+\pi/4)[u^\mathrm{T}\{g_y(W)-g_y(\widetilde W)\}]^2\).
Independence of \(W\) and \(\widetilde W\) therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E k_{u,\widetilde W}^2
 =\left(6+\frac\pi2\right)
   \operatorname{Var}(u^\mathrm{T} g_y(W))
 \le Cs\,u^\mathrm{T}(I-\Sigma_y)u,
 \label{flux:eq:forcing-moment}
\end{equation}
where the last step is \cref{flux:eq:conditional-identities}.

Insert fresh Gaussian momentum in \cref{flux:eq:halfturn-duhamel}, average
the independent reference, and discard the terminal momentum.  Jensen's
inequality, semigroup contractivity, and
\(\int_0^{T_\gamma}|B_\gamma(r)|\,\mathrm{d} r\le C\) yield
\[
 \lVert(I+F_y^w)\ell_{u,y}\rVert_2^2
 \le C\left\{\gamma^2u^\mathrm{T}\Sigma_yu
                   +\mathbb E k_{u,\widetilde W}^2\right\}.
\]
Here the norm is in \(L^2(q_y^w)\), and the remaining expectation includes
the independent position, reference, and Gaussian momentum.
The parameter choice in \cref{sec:flux} gives
\(\gamma^2\le as/(1+a)\).  Since
\(I-\Sigma_y\succeq a(1+a)^{-1}I\) and \(\Sigma_y\preceq I\), the
damping term is at most
\(s u^\mathrm{T}(I-\Sigma_y)u\).  Combining this with
\cref{flux:eq:forcing-moment} proves
\cref{flux:eq:weighted-halfturn}.

label: flux:lem:outer-geometry
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{flux:lem:outer-geometry}
If \(s\le1/3\), then \(\mathsf T\) is self-adjoint and, on
\(\mathcal H_Y\),
\begin{equation}
 -\tfrac12I\preceq\mathsf T
 \preceq\frac{1-a}{1+a}I,
 \qquad
 \Gamma\succeq\gamma_a I,
 \qquad \gamma_a=\frac{2\sqrt a}{1+a}.
 \label{flux:eq:outer-spectrum}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\(4\eta\lVert\nabla\mathsf T f\rVert^2\le\lVert\Gamma f\rVert^2\), and
\(\mathsf C=\mathsf V\Gamma\) for an isometry
\(\mathsf V:\mathcal H_Y\to\operatorname{ran}(\mathsf Q)\).
head: environment
name: Outer-reflection geometry

title: Proof
body_md:
Exchangeability of \((Y_+,Y_-)\) makes \(\mathsf T\) self-adjoint.
The conditional density of \(Y_-\) given \(Y_+=y\) is proportional to
\[
 \exp\left\{-V\left(\frac{y+u}{2}\right)
              -\frac{\lVerty-u\rVert^2}{8\eta}\right\}.
\]
Its curvature in \(u\) is at least
\((\alpha+\eta^{-1})I/4\), while the derivative with respect to \(u\)
of its \(y\)-score has norm at most \((\eta^{-1}-\alpha)/4\).
Conditional Brascamp--Lieb therefore gives
\[
 \eta\lVert\nabla\mathsf T f\rVert^2
 \le\frac{(1-a)^2}{4(1+a)}\lVert\mathsf C f\rVert^2
 \le\frac14\lVert\Gamma f\rVert^2.
\]
The \(Y\)-marginal has Poincar\'e constant at most
\(\alpha^{-1}+\eta\) by \cref{flux:lem:conditional-geometry}.  Applying
this inequality to the centered function \(\mathsf Tf\) and using
\(\lVertf\rVert^2=\lVert\mathsf Tf\rVert^2+\lVert\mathsf Cf\rVert^2\) gives
\(\lVert\mathsf T\rVert\le(1-a)/(1+a)\).

For the lower spectral edge, exchangeability and Gaussian Poincar\'e give
\(\langle h,(I-\mathsf T)h\rangle\le2\eta\lVert\nabla h\rVert^2\).
Apply this with \(h=\mathsf Tf\) and use the preceding derivative bound.
Spectral calculus yields
\((I-\mathsf T)^2(I+2\mathsf T)\succeq0\), hence
\(\mathsf T\succeq-I/2\).  Because
\((1-a)/(1+a)\ge1/2\), these two edges imply the stated lower bound on
\(\Gamma\).  Finally, unitarity of \(\mathsf U\) gives
\(\mathsf C^*\mathsf C=I-\mathsf T^2=\Gamma^2\), so
\(\mathsf V=\mathsf C\Gamma^{-1}\) is an isometry.

 The weak-gradient and spectral-domain justification for this calculation
 is given in \cref{flux:app:regularity}.

label: flux:lem:affine-after-reflection
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{flux:lem:affine-after-reflection}
There is an error \(e_f\), centered conditionally on \(Y_+\), such that
\(\mathsf C f=L_f+e_f\).  If
\[
 \mathcal R_f=\lVert\nabla f\rVert^2-\lVert\mathsf T\nabla f\rVert^2,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_f=\mathbb E[b_{Y_+}^\mathrm{T}(I-\Sigma_{Y_+})b_{Y_+}],
\]
then, for sufficiently small universal \(s\),
\begin{equation}
 \lVerte_f\rVert^2\le4\eta\mathcal R_f,\qquad
 \mathcal R_f+\mathcal D_f
 \le C\lVert\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert\lVert\nabla f\rVert.
 \label{flux:eq:affine-reflection-control}
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Affine approximation after reflection

title: Proof
body_md:
Here \(\mathsf T\nabla f\) means that \(\mathsf T\) is applied to every
coordinate of the vector-valued gradient; in particular,
\((\mathsf T\nabla f)(y)=b_y\).
Conditionally on \(Y_+=y\),
\(Y_-=y+2\sqrt\eta W\).  Subtracting its best first-order conditional
approximation gives
\[
 e_f=f(Y_-)-\mathsf Tf(Y_+)
       -2\sqrt\eta\,b_{Y_+}^\mathrm{T}(W-\bar w_{Y_+}).
\]
Conditional Poincar\'e proves
\(\lVerte_f\rVert^2\le4\eta\mathcal R_f\).

For the second estimate, differentiate the conditional expectation
weakly.  Integration by parts and
\cref{flux:eq:conditional-identities} give
\[
 \nabla(I-\mathsf T)f
 =\nabla f-b_y+2(I-\Sigma_y)b_y
 +\eta^{-1/2}\operatorname{Cov}(e_f,g_y(W)\mid Y_+=y).
\]
In this identity, \(\nabla f\) on the right is evaluated at \(y\), and the
conditional covariance is over \(W\) given \(Y_+=y\).  Write
\(b(y)=b_y\).
Take its inner product with \(\nabla f+b_y\) and average over \(y\).
The first term gives \(\mathcal R_f\), and the leading covariance term
gives \(4\mathcal D_f\).  Also, the spectral lower bound
\(\mathsf T\succeq-I/2\) implies
\[
 \lVert\nabla f-b\rVert^2
 \le3\{\lVert\nabla f\rVert^2-\lVertb\rVert^2\}=3\mathcal R_f,
\]
The two remaining cross terms are bounded using this inequality,
\cref{flux:eq:conditional-identities}, the first inequality in
\cref{flux:eq:affine-reflection-control}, and
\(I-\Sigma_y\preceq sI\).  They are at most
\[
 C\sqrt{s\mathcal R_f\mathcal D_f}
 +C\sqrt{s\mathcal R_f(s\mathcal R_f+\mathcal D_f)}.
\]
The leading inner product is at most
\(2\lVert\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert\lVert\nabla f\rVert\).
Young's inequality absorbs the displayed cross terms when \(s\) is
sufficiently small.  The graph-norm extension to the stated weak-gradient
domain is recorded in \cref{flux:app:regularity}.

label: flux:lem:dyadic-comparison
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{flux:lem:dyadic-comparison}
Suppose \(mI\preceq B\preceq MI\) and a bounded operator \(A\) satisfies
\(\lVertAv\rVert^2\le\lVertv\rVert\lVertBv\rVert\).  Then
\[
 A^*A\preceq C\{1+\log(M/m)\}B.
\]
head: environment
name: Dyadic operator comparison

title: Proof
body_md:
Partition the spectrum of \(B\) into dyadic intervals and write
\(v=\sum_{j=1}^Jv_j\), where
\(J\le C\{1+\log(M/m)\}\).  If \(\lambda_j\) is the lower endpoint of
the \(j\)-th interval, then the hypothesis gives
\(\lVertAv_j\rVert\le\sqrt{2\lambda_j}\lVertv_j\rVert\).  Consequently,
\[
 \lVertAv\rVert^2
 \le J\sum_j2\lambda_j\lVertv_j\rVert^2
 \le2J\langle v,Bv\rangle,
\]
which proves the claim.

label: flux:prop:global-halfturn
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Global half-turn estimate

title: Proof
body_md:
First restrict \(f\) to the spectral subspace of \(\mathsf T\)
corresponding to \([1/2,1]\).  Apply
\cref{flux:prop:weighted-affine} conditionally to the affine part \(L_f\)
of \(\mathsf Cf\), use
\(\lVertI+\mathsf F_Q\rVert\le2\) on \(e_f\), and then apply
\cref{flux:lem:affine-after-reflection}.  This gives
\[
 \lVert(I+\mathsf F_Q)\mathsf C f\rVert^2
 \le C\eta\lVert\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert\lVert\nabla f\rVert.
\]
On this spectral subspace, applying the derivative estimate in
\cref{flux:lem:outer-geometry} to \(\mathsf T^{-1}f\) and
\(\mathsf T^{-1}(I-\mathsf T)f\) gives
\[
 \sqrt\eta\lVert\nabla f\rVert\le C\lVert\Gamma f\rVert,
 \qquad
 \sqrt\eta\lVert\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert
 \le C\lVert\Gamma^3f\rVert.
\]
Since \(\mathsf C=\mathsf V\Gamma\), setting
\(f=\Gamma^{-1}v\), which is allowed by
\(\Gamma\succeq\gamma_aI\), shows that
\(\mathsf A_{\rm ht}=(I+\mathsf F_Q)\mathsf V\) obeys
\(\lVert\mathsf A_{\rm ht}v\rVert^2
\le C\lVertv\rVert\lVert\Gamma^2v\rVert\).
Applying \cref{flux:lem:dyadic-comparison} to
\(A=\mathsf A_{\rm ht}\), \(B=\Gamma^2\), and
\(m=\gamma_a^2\) gives the required bound without treating the generally
non-self-adjoint half-turn error \(\mathsf A_{\rm ht}\) as a positive
operator.

On the complementary spectral subspace,
\(\Gamma^2\succeq3I/4\), while \(\lVert\mathsf A_{\rm ht}\rVert\le2\), so the result
is immediate.  The two output vectors need not be orthogonal; the triangle
inequality and
\(\lVertr_1+r_2\rVert^2\le2\lVertr_1\rVert^2+2\lVertr_2\rVert^2\) prove
\cref{flux:eq:global-halfturn} for an arbitrary \(v\).

label: flux:lem:one-step-energy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{flux:lem:one-step-energy}
Let
\[
 \Lambda_\rho=\log(\mathrm{e}/\gamma_a)+(\rho/\gamma_a)^2,
 \qquad \vartheta=c_\star\rho/\Lambda_\rho
\]
for a sufficiently small universal \(c_\star\).  If
\(0<\rho\le1/2\), then
\[
 \tfrac12\lVertf\rVert^2\le\mathcal E_\vartheta(f)
 \le\tfrac32\lVertf\rVert^2,
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_\vartheta(\mathsf Kf)
 \le\left(1-c\frac\rho{\Lambda_\rho}\right)
       \mathcal E_\vartheta(f).
\]
head: environment
name: One-step energy decay

title: Proof
body_md:
Because \(\mathsf T\) commutes with \(\Gamma\), the block operator
associated with \(2\mathcal C\) has square
\(\operatorname{diag}(\Gamma^{-2},\Gamma^{-2})\).  Hence
\(\lvert\mathcal C\rvert\le(2\gamma_a)^{-1}
(\lVertf_Y\rVert^2+\lVertf_V\rVert^2)\).  The displayed choice of \(\vartheta\)
satisfies \(\vartheta\le\gamma_a\), proving energy equivalence.

From \cref{flux:eq:ideal-operator} and contractivity of
\(\mathsf F_Q\),
\begin{equation}
 \lVert\mathsf Kf\rVert^2-\lVertf\rVert^2\le-\rho\lVertf_Q\rVert^2.
 \label{flux:eq:refresh-dissipation}
\end{equation}
To see how the correction changes, first replace the conditional move by
an exact sign reversal and set
\(g=\mathsf U(\mathsf P-\mathsf Q)f\).  Unitarity of \(\mathsf U\) and
\(\mathsf C=\mathsf V\Gamma\) give
\[
 \binom{g_Y}{g_V}
 =\begin{pmatrix}\mathsf T&-\Gamma\\
                  \Gamma&\mathsf T\end{pmatrix}
  \binom{f_Y}{f_V},
 \qquad
 \mathcal C(g_Y,g_V)-\mathcal C(f_Y,f_V)
 =-\lVertf_Y\rVert^2+\lVertf_V\rVert^2.
\]

The actual conditional move differs from this sign reversal by
\[
 e_{\rm ht}=\mathsf V^*(I+\mathsf F_Q)f_Q,
 \qquad e_\rho=\rho f_V+(1-\rho)e_{\rm ht}.
\]
The two tracked components of the actual update are
\((\mathsf Kf)_Y=g_Y+\Gamma e_\rho\) and
\((\mathsf Kf)_V=g_V-\mathsf T e_\rho\).  Direct substitution gives
\[
 \mathcal C((\mathsf Kf)_Y,(\mathsf Kf)_V)-\mathcal C(f_Y,f_V)
 =-\lVertf_Y\rVert^2+\lVertf_V\rVert^2
  +\langle g_Y,\Gamma^{-1}e_\rho\rangle
  +\tfrac12\lVerte_\rho\rVert^2.
\]
By \cref{flux:prop:global-halfturn},
\(\mathsf A_{\rm ht}^*\mathsf A_{\rm ht}
\preceq C\log(\mathrm{e}/\gamma_a)\Gamma^2\) for
\(\mathsf A_{\rm ht}=(I+\mathsf F_Q)\mathsf V\).  The corresponding
operator factorization gives a bounded \(B\), with
\(\lVertB\rVert^2\le C\log(\mathrm{e}/\gamma_a)\), such that
\(\mathsf A_{\rm ht}=B\Gamma\).  Since
\(e_{\rm ht}=\mathsf A_{\rm ht}^*f_Q\), this gives
\(\lVert\Gamma^{-1}e_{\rm ht}\rVert^2
\le C\log(\mathrm{e}/\gamma_a)\lVertf_Q\rVert^2\).  Therefore
\(\lVert\Gamma^{-1}e_\rho\rVert^2
\le C\Lambda_\rho\lVertf_Q\rVert^2\), while
\(\lVerte_\rho\rVert\le2\lVertf_Q\rVert\).  Young's inequality now yields
\[
 \mathcal C((\mathsf Kf)_Y,(\mathsf Kf)_V)-\mathcal C(f_Y,f_V)
 \le-\tfrac12\lVertf_Y\rVert^2+C\Lambda_\rho\lVertf_Q\rVert^2.
\]
Multiply by \(\vartheta\), add
\cref{flux:eq:refresh-dissipation}, and choose \(c_\star\) small enough.
Energy equivalence then proves the claimed one-step decay.

head: environment
name: Finite compiler at a fixed step size

label: flux:lem:clock-coupling
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{flux:lem:clock-coupling}
Conditionally on \(Y=y\), let \(X,\widetilde X\) be independent draws from
\(q_y\), and let \(P\sim\gamma_d\) be independent.  Then, for universal
\(c,C>0\) and every \(u\ge0\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\sqrt\eta
 [P^\mathrm{T}\{\nabla V(X)-\nabla V(\widetilde X)\}]_+
 >Cs(\sqrt{du}+u)\right\}\le C\mathrm{e}^{-cu}.
\]
If, in addition, \(s\sqrt d\) is below a universal constant, then an
augmented initial law \(\nu\) satisfying
\(D_2(\nu\Vert\Pi_\eta)\le\Delta\) admits the following consequence: for
every \(\xi\in(0,1/2)\), the exact and capped half-turns can be coupled to
agree with probability at least \(1-\xi\), using
\[
 \bar\lambda_{\xi,\Delta}
 =Cs\{\sqrt{d\ell_{\xi,\Delta}}+\ell_{\xi,\Delta}\},
 \qquad
 \ell_{\xi,\Delta}=C\{\Delta+\log(1/\xi)\}.
\]
The capped half-turn uses exactly
\(T_\gamma\bar\lambda_{\xi,\Delta}\) candidate events in expectation.
head: environment
name: Stationary rate tail and clock coupling

title: Proof
body_md:
The conditional law is
\((\alpha+\eta^{-1})\)-strongly log-concave.  Norm concentration and its
second-moment bound show that, outside an event of probability
\(2\mathrm{e}^{-u}\), both
\(\lVertX-\mathbb E X\rVert\) and \(\lVert\widetilde X-\mathbb E X\rVert\) are at most
\(C\sqrt{\eta(d+u)}\).
Smoothness then bounds the conditional standard deviation of the scalar
product with \(P\) by \(Cs(\sqrt d+\sqrt u)\).  A Gaussian tail bound
proves the displayed estimate.  Integrating it above
\(Cs(\sqrt{d\ell}+\ell)\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E(\lambda-\bar\lambda)_+
 \le Cs(\sqrt d+\ell+1)\mathrm{e}^{-c\ell}.
\]

Under \(\Pi_\eta\), invariance from
\cref{flux:prop:fixed-validity} makes this bound valid at every time.
Couple the exact and capped clocks with the same Poisson random measure;
they separate only if an excess-rate event occurs.  Taking
\(\ell=C\{\Delta+\log(1/\xi)\}\) makes the stationary separation
probability at most \(\mathrm{e}^{-\Delta}\xi^2\).  Under a \(D_2\)-warm initial
law, the path likelihood ratio is only its initial density ratio, since all
subsequent references, Gaussian noise, clocks, and marks use common
kernels.  Cauchy--Schwarz therefore raises the stationary failure
probability by at most \(\mathrm{e}^{\Delta/2}\), giving \(\xi\).  The final
expectation is that of a homogeneous Poisson clock on an interval of length
\(T_\gamma=O(1)\).

label: flux:prop:rgo
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{flux:prop:rgo}
There is a universal \(K_{\rm rgo}\) such that the following holds.  Given
\(y\), \(0<\delta<1/2\), and a point \(\widehat x\) satisfying
\[
 \lVerty-\eta\nabla V(\widehat x)-\widehat x\rVert\le\sqrt{d\eta},
\]
if
\[
 \eta^{-1}\ge K_{\rm rgo}\beta
 \{\sqrt{d\log(1/\delta)}+\log(1/\delta)\},
\]
the rejection sampler of
\citet[Theorems~3.1 and D.1]{chen2026high} returns a law
\(\widehat q_y\) satisfying
\[
 \chi^2(\widehat q_y\Vert q_y)\le\delta^2,\qquad
 \chi^2(q_y\Vert\widehat q_y)\le\delta^2,
\]
using at most \(K_{\rm rgo}\) expected oracle queries after construction
of the displayed certificate.
head: environment
name: Approximate RGO

title: Proof
body_md:
Augmentation preserves warmness:
\[
 \frac{\mathrm{d}\operatorname{Law}(X_0,Y_0)}{\mathrm{d}\Pi_\eta}(x,y)
 =\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu_0}{\mathrm{d}\pi}(x),\qquad
 D_2(\operatorname{Law}(X_0,Y_0)\Vert\Pi_\eta)\le\Delta.
\]
\Cref{flux:thm:ideal} and the choice of \(M\) put the ideal output within
\(\varepsilon/2\) of \(\pi\).  Because every ideal row preserves \(\Pi_\eta\),
data processing keeps its intermediate \(D_2\) divergence at most
\(\Delta\).

It remains to couple every finite row to its ideal counterpart.  There are
three possible disagreements.

\emph{Center cap.}
Under stationarity, write \(Y=X+\sqrt\eta Z\).  After reflection, the
normalized residual at the incoming position is
\[
 \frac{\lVert\sqrt\eta Z+\eta\nabla V(X)\rVert}{\sqrt{d\eta}}.
\]
Strong log-concavity, Gaussian concentration, and
\(\lVert\nabla V(X)\rVert\le\beta\lVertX-x^\star\rVert\), where \(x^\star\) minimizes
\(V\), show that it exceeds
\(2\sqrt\kappa(1+\sqrt{2u/d})\) with probability at most \(2\mathrm{e}^{-u}\).
Taking
\(u=\Delta+2\log(1/\delta_{\rm row})+\log2\) and using
\cref{flux:eq:center-cost} shows that the stationary cap-failure
probability is at most \(\mathrm{e}^{-\Delta}\delta_{\rm row}^2\).  The warm-path
Cauchy--Schwarz argument used in \cref{flux:lem:clock-coupling} makes it at
most \(\delta_{\rm row}\) under the current ideal law.

\emph{Approximate reference.}
The definitions imply
\(\log(1/\delta_{\rm row})\le C\ell\).  The gate
\cref{flux:eq:finite-gate} therefore implies the small-step-size condition in
\cref{flux:prop:rgo}.  Either directed \(\chi^2\) bound implies total
variation at most \(\delta_{\rm row}/2\), so maximal coupling matches the
approximate and exact references except with probability at most
\(\delta_{\rm row}\).  Because all laws have Borel densities on
\(\mathbb R^d\), these maximal couplings may be selected jointly measurably in
\(y\).  On agreement, the same draw is used in both chains.

\emph{Capped clock.}
The same parameter bound gives
\(\ell_{\delta_{\rm row},\Delta}\le C\ell\).  After increasing \(K\),
\cref{flux:lem:clock-coupling}, applied conditionally on the common
pre-row history, couples the exact and capped half-turns with failure
probability at most \(\delta_{\rm row}\).

A union bound over three events and \(M\) rows is at most \(\varepsilon/2\).
Together with the ideal mixing error, this proves the total-variation
claim.

Early termination only reduces work.  Each row uses at most
\(Q_{\rm ctr}\) center queries, a universal expected number of RGO
queries, one query to cache \(\nabla V(\widetilde X)\) on the half-turn branch, and
\(T_\gamma\bar\lambda\) expected event-test queries.  Hence
\[
 \mathbb E N_{\mathrm{qry}}
 \le CM\{Q_{\rm ctr}+s(\sqrt{d\ell}+\ell)\},
\]
which is \cref{flux:eq:fixed-scale-cost}.

label: persistent:lem:fixed-invariance
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:fixed-invariance}
For every fixed \(y,e\), \cref{eq:persistent-generator} defines a
non-explosive Markov process.  If \(S_t^{y,e}\) denotes its transition
operator and \(\mathsf R(w,p)=(w,-p)\), then
\[
 q_y^w\otimes\gamma_d\text{ is invariant},
 \qquad (S_t^{y,e})^*=\mathsf R S_t^{y,e}\mathsf R .
\]
Both conclusions remain valid after averaging \(S_t^{y,e}\) over any
measurable reference law depending on \(y\), provided the reference is
conditionally independent of the incoming \((W,P)\).
head: environment
name: Fixed-reference validity

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(a=b_y(e)\), \(r(w)=b_y(w)-a\), and
\[
 \mathsf J(w,p)=(w,\operatorname{Ref}_{r(w)}p),
 \qquad s(w,p)=p^\mathrm{T} r(w).
\]
Between events the process follows the harmonic flow
\[
 \phi_u(w,p)=\bigl(-a+(w+a)\cos u+p\sin u,
                    -(w+a)\sin u+p\cos u\bigr).
\]
Both this flow and \(\mathsf J\) preserve
\(H(w,p)=\{\lVertw+a\rVert^2+\lVertp\rVert^2\}/2\).  Thus every set
\(K_R=\{H\le R\}\) is invariant.  Lipschitz continuity of \(b_y\) bounds
the event rate \(\lambda=[s]_+\) on \(K_R\) by
\[
 \lVertp\rVert\,\lVertb_y(w)-b_y(e)\rVert
 \le\beta\eta\sqrt{2R}\{\sqrt{2R}+\lVerte+a\rVert\}
 =:\Lambda_R.
\]
Thinning a homogeneous Poisson process of rate \(\Lambda_R\) therefore
constructs the process from every point of \(K_R\).  Since every initial
state lies in some \(K_R\), this proves well-posedness and non-explosion.

We prove skew balance directly on paths.  The idea is to pair every path with
its time reversal after flipping momentum: collision factors agree one by
one, while the change in target density exactly cancels the change in the
survival probability.  Write \(z=(w,p)\), set
\[
 \Psi(w)=V(y+\sqrt\eta w)-a^\mathrm{T} w,
 \qquad \nu=q_y^w\otimes\gamma_d,
\]
so that the Lebesgue density of \(\nu\) is, up to normalization,
\(\varrho(z)=\exp\{-H(z)-\Psi(w)\}\).  Along a flight,
\(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} u}\Psi(w_u)=s(z_u)\), while a collision changes neither
\(H\) nor \(\Psi\).  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf R\phi_u\mathsf R=\phi_{-u},\qquad
 \mathsf J\mathsf R=\mathsf R\mathsf J,\qquad
 s\circ\mathsf J=s\circ\mathsf R=-s.
 \label{persistent:eq:path-reversal-identities}
\end{equation}

Fix \(t>0\).  For
\(\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) in the ordered simplex
\(\Delta_n(t)=\{0<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t\}\), let
\(z_u=z_u(z_0,\boldsymbol t)\) be the deterministic skeleton obtained by
following \(\phi\) and inserting a collision \(\mathsf J\) at every
\(t_i\).  On \(K_R\), the iterated-hazard expansion of the transition
operator is
\begin{equation}
 S_t^{y,e}F(z_0)
 =\sum_{n\ge0}\int_{\Delta_n(t)}
   \exp\!\left\{-\int_0^t\lambda(z_u)\,\mathrm{d} u\right\}
   \prod_{i=1}^n\lambda(z_{t_i-})F(z_t)\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol t .
 \label{persistent:eq:ordered-event-expansion}
\end{equation}
The bound by \(\Lambda_R\) makes this series absolutely convergent.

Pair this skeleton with the one starting at \(\mathsf Rz_t\) and having
ordered collision times
\((t-t_n,\ldots,t-t_1)\).  By
\cref{persistent:eq:path-reversal-identities}, it is the momentum-reversed
time reversal of the original skeleton and ends at \(\mathsf Rz_0\).  The
map
\[
 (z_0,t_1,\ldots,t_n)
 \longmapsto(\mathsf Rz_t,t-t_n,\ldots,t-t_1)
\]
preserves Lebesgue measure.  Indeed, \(\phi_u\) and \(\mathsf R\) preserve
volume, while \(\mathsf J\) does so by applying, for every fixed \(w\), an
orthogonal change of variables in \(p\).  This argument does not require
continuity of the reflection direction at \(r(w)=0\), where the event rate
vanishes.

If \(z^-\) is a forward pre-collision state, the corresponding reverse
pre-collision state is \(\mathsf R\mathsf Jz^-\); hence
\[
 \lambda(\mathsf R\mathsf Jz^-)=\lambda(z^-).
\]
Thus the collision-rate products in
\cref{persistent:eq:ordered-event-expansion} agree.  The reverse survival
hazard is \(\int_0^t[-s(z_u)]_+\,\mathrm{d} u\), and
\[
 \Psi(w_t)-\Psi(w_0)
 =\int_0^t s(z_u)\,\mathrm{d} u
 =\int_0^t\bigl\{[s(z_u)]_+-[-s(z_u)]_+\bigr\}\,\mathrm{d} u.
\]
Since \(H(z_t)=H(z_0)\) and \(\varrho(\mathsf Rz)=\varrho(z)\), this is
exactly the survival-weight identity
\begin{equation}
 \varrho(z_0)\exp\!\left\{-\int_0^t[s(z_u)]_+\,\mathrm{d} u\right\}
 =\varrho(\mathsf Rz_t)
  \exp\!\left\{-\int_0^t[-s(z_u)]_+\,\mathrm{d} u\right\}.
 \label{persistent:eq:path-weight-balance}
\end{equation}

Let \(\nu_R\) be \(\nu\) conditioned on \(K_R\).  Pairing paths term by
term in \cref{persistent:eq:ordered-event-expansion} using
\cref{persistent:eq:path-weight-balance} gives, for bounded measurable
\(F,G\),
\[
 \int F S_t^{y,e}G\,\mathrm{d}\nu_R
 =\int (\mathsf R G)S_t^{y,e}(\mathsf R F)\,\mathrm{d}\nu_R
 =\int (\mathsf R S_t^{y,e}\mathsf R F)G\,\mathrm{d}\nu_R.
\]
Letting \(R\to\infty\) gives the same identity under \(\nu\).  Taking
\(F=1\) proves invariance.  Jensen's inequality then makes
\(S_t^{y,e}\) a contraction on \(L^2(\nu)\), and density of bounded
functions extends the identity to \(L^2(\nu)\), proving
\((S_t^{y,e})^*=\mathsf R S_t^{y,e}\mathsf R\).

Finally, the recursive hazard construction is jointly Borel in
\((y,e,z_0)\): the flow, rate, integrated hazard, and reflection are Borel,
and successive event times are obtained by taking level-hitting times of
the integrated hazard.  Non-explosion gives the measurable pointwise
limit.  Consequently, conditioning on an incoming-state-independent
reference and applying Fubini passes both invariance and the adjoint
identity to every measurable reference mixture.

\label{persistent:lem:closed-gradient-smoothing}
The set \(\mathcal C_0\) is a graph core for \(D\).  Suppose that
\(\mathsf T\) is a self-adjoint contraction,
\(\mathsf T\mathcal C_0\subset\operatorname{Dom}(D)\), and, on
\(\mathcal C_0\),
\begin{equation}
 \sqrt\eta\lVertD\mathsf T u\rVert\le c_D\lVert\Gamma u\rVert.
 \label{persistent:eq:core-smoothing}
\end{equation}
Then \(D\mathsf T\) has an everywhere-defined bounded extension
\(\mathsf R_D:L^2_0(\nu)\to L^2(\nu;\mathbb R^d)\), and in fact
\[
 \mathsf T L^2_0(\nu)\subset\operatorname{Dom}(D),\qquad
 D\mathsf T=\mathsf R_D,\qquad
 \sqrt\eta\lVert\mathsf R_Du\rVert\le c_D\lVert\Gamma u\rVert.
\]
Consequently, if
\(\Pi_+=\mathbf1_{[1/2,1]}(\mathsf T)\), then
\(\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_+)\subset\operatorname{Dom}(D)\) and
\begin{align*}
 \sqrt\eta\lVertDf\rVert&\le2c_D\lVert\Gamma f\rVert,
                                               
 \\
 \sqrt\eta\lVertD(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert
 &\le2c_D\lVert\Gamma^3f\rVert,
 \qquad f\in\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_+).
                                                 
\end{align*}
Moreover, for every \(f\in\operatorname{Dom}(D)\),
\begin{equation}
 D(I-\mathsf T)f=Df-\mathsf R_Df.
 \label{persistent:eq:graph-difference}
\end{equation}
Thus convergence in the graph norm of \(D\) automatically implies
convergence of \(D(I-\mathsf T)f\); no additional graph norm is needed.
head: environment
name: Closed weak-gradient smoothing

title: Proof
body_md:
The density of \(\nu\) is positive and continuous, hence is bounded above
and below on every compact set.  Cutoff followed by ordinary convolution
therefore approximates every element of \(\operatorname{Dom}(D)\) in the
norm \(\lVertf\rVert^2+\lVertDf\rVert^2\).  To preserve centering, subtract the mean
of each approximant times a fixed \(\psi\in C_c^\infty\) satisfying
\(\int\psi\,\mathrm{d}\nu=1\).  This proves the graph-core assertion.

If \(u_n\in\mathcal C_0\) converges in \(L^2(\nu)\),
\cref{persistent:eq:core-smoothing} makes \(D\mathsf T u_n\) Cauchy,
while \(\mathsf T u_n\) converges.  Closedness of \(D\) shows that the
limit belongs to \(\operatorname{Dom}(D)\), identifies its gradient, and
gives the bounded extension \(\mathsf R_D=D\mathsf T\).

On \(\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_+)\), \(\mathsf T^{-1}\) is bounded with
norm at most two.  For \(f\) in that subspace,
\[
 Df=\mathsf R_D\mathsf T^{-1}f,
 \qquad
 D(I-\mathsf T)f
 =\mathsf R_D\mathsf T^{-1}(I-\mathsf T)f.
\]
The first estimate follows from
\(\gamma_t/t\le2\gamma_t\) on \(t\in[1/2,1]\), where
\(\gamma_t=(1-t^2)^{1/2}\).  The second follows from
\[
 \frac{1-t}{t}=\frac{1-t^2}{t(1+t)}\le2(1-t^2),
 \qquad t\in[1/2,1].
\]
Finally, \(\mathsf T f\in\operatorname{Dom}(D)\) for every
\(f\in L^2_0(\nu)\),
so \cref{persistent:eq:graph-difference} follows by linearity and proves
the last assertion.
head: environment

label: persistent:lem:outer-geometry
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:outer-geometry}
Assume \(\beta\eta\le1/3\).  On \(\mathcal H_Y\),
\[
 -\tfrac12 I\preceq\mathsf T
 \preceq\frac{1-g^2}{1+g^2}I,\qquad
 \Gamma\succeq\frac{2g}{1+g^2}I.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathsf C:=\mathsf Q\mathsf U\mathsf P\) can be written as
\(\mathsf C=\mathsf V\Gamma\), where \(\mathsf V\) is an isometry, and
\[
 \mathsf U\mathsf P f=\mathsf P\mathsf T f+\mathsf V\Gamma f,\qquad
 \mathsf U\mathsf V f=\mathsf P\Gamma f-\mathsf V\mathsf T f.
\]
On \(\mathcal H_+\),
\[
 \sqrt\eta\lVert\nabla f\rVert\le C\lVert\Gamma f\rVert,\qquad
 \sqrt\eta\lVert\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert
 \le C\lVert\Gamma^3f\rVert.
\]
head: environment
name: Outer-reflection geometry

title: Proof
body_md:
The pair \((Y_+,Y_-)\) is exchangeable and
\((\mathsf Tf)(y)=\mathbb E[f(Y_-)\mid Y_+=y]\), so \(\mathsf T\) is a
self-adjoint contraction.  The conditional density of \(Y_-\) given
\(Y_+=y\) is proportional to
\[
 \exp\left\{-V\left(\frac{y+u}{2}\right)
             -\frac{\lVerty-u\rVert^2}{8\eta}\right\}.
\]
Its score with respect to \(y\) is
\(s_y(u)=-\nabla V((y+u)/2)/2-(y-u)/(4\eta)\).  For
\(f\in\mathcal C_0\), weak differentiation under the integral gives
\[
 D\mathsf Tf(y)
 =\operatorname{Cov}(f(Y_-),s_y(Y_-)\mid Y_+=y).
\]
Indeed, on compact sets of \(y\), the score times the conditional density
is dominated by an integrable Gaussian tail.  Thus Fubini and weak
integration by parts justify differentiation of both the numerator and
normalizing constant.  In particular,
\(\mathsf T\mathcal C_0\subset\operatorname{Dom}(D)\).
Applying conditional Poincar\'e to this covariance gives
\[
 \eta\lVertD\mathsf Tf\rVert^2
 \le\frac{(1-\alpha\eta)^2}{4(1+\alpha\eta)}
       \{\lVertf\rVert^2-\lVert\mathsf Tf\rVert^2\}
 \le\frac14\lVert\Gamma f\rVert^2.
\]
The \(Y\)-marginal has Poincar\'e constant at most
\(\alpha^{-1}+\eta\): this follows from the conditional covariance bound
\(\operatorname{Cov}(X\mid Y)\preceq\eta(1+\alpha\eta)^{-1}I\) and
Brascamp--Lieb \citep{chewi2023log}.  Equivalently, if \(W_\eta\) is the
negative log-density of the \(Y\)-marginal, then
\[
 \nabla^2W_\eta(y)
 =\eta^{-1}I-\eta^{-2}\operatorname{Cov}(X\mid Y=y)
 \succeq\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha\eta}I.
\]
Applying the resulting Poincar\'e inequality to the
centered function \(\mathsf Tf\) yields
\(\lVert\mathsf T\rVert_{L^2_0}\le(1-g^2)/(1+g^2)\).
This inequality is first obtained on \(\mathcal C_0\) and extends to
\(L^2_0(\nu)\) by density.

For the lower edge, exchangeability and Gaussian Poincar\'e imply
\[
 \langleh,(I-\mathsf T)h\rangle
 =\tfrac12\mathbb E\{h(Y_+)-h(Y_-)\}^2
 \le2\eta\lVert\nabla h\rVert^2.
\]
Take \(h=\mathsf Tf\) for \(f\in\mathcal C_0\) and use the preceding
derivative bound.  The resulting inequality involves only bounded
polynomials in \(\mathsf T\), so density extends it to all of
\(L^2_0(\nu)\).  Spectral calculus gives
\(2\mathsf T^2(I-\mathsf T)\preceq I-\mathsf T^2\), equivalently
\((I-\mathsf T)^2(I+2\mathsf T)\succeq0\), and hence
\(\mathsf T\succeq-I/2\).  The two spectral edges imply the lower bound
on \(\Gamma\).  Since \(\mathsf T1=1\), the lower bound
\(\mathsf T\succeq-I/2\) also holds on the full scalar \(L^2(\nu)\), and
hence coordinatewise on vector fields such as \(Df\), whose components
need not be centered.

Finally,
\(\mathsf C^*\mathsf C=I-\mathsf T^2=\Gamma^2\).  Thus
\(\mathsf V=\mathsf C\Gamma^{-1}\) is an isometry, and
\(\mathsf U^2=I\) gives the two block identities.

The core derivative estimate above is
\cref{persistent:eq:core-smoothing} with \(c_D=1/2\).  Applying
\cref{persistent:lem:closed-gradient-smoothing} proves that all of
\(\mathcal H_+\), not merely a smooth subset of it, belongs to the weak
gradient domain and gives the two final inequalities.  Notice that this
argument never applies the discontinuous spectral projection \(\Pi_+\) to
a smooth function.
head: environment

label: persistent:lem:affine-control
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:affine-control}
For every \(f\in\mathcal C_0\),
\(\mathsf Q\mathsf U\mathsf P f=L_f+e_f\), where
\(\mathbb E[e_f\mid Y_+]=0\).  With
\[
 \mathcal R_f=\lVert\nabla f\rVert^2-\lVert\mathsf T\nabla f\rVert^2,\qquad
 \mathcal D_f=\mathbb E[a_f(Y_+)^\mathrm{T} D_{Y_+}a_f(Y_+)],
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \lVerte_f\rVert^2\le4\eta\mathcal R_f,\qquad
 \mathcal R_f+\mathcal D_f
 \le C\lVert\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert\lVert\nabla f\rVert.
 \label{persistent:eq:affine-control}
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Affine approximation after reflection

title: Proof
body_md:
Conditionally on \(Y_+=y\), we have
\(Y_-=y+2\sqrt\eta W\).  Set
\(e_f=\mathsf Q\mathsf U\mathsf Pf-L_f\).  The choice of \(a_f(y)\)
makes both \(\mathbb E[e_f\mid Y_+=y]\) and
\(\mathbb E[\nabla_We_f\mid Y_+=y]\) zero.
The conditional position law is one-strongly log-concave in \(W\), so
conditional Poincar\'e gives the first inequality.

For the second, let
\(b_y(w)=\sqrt\eta\,\nabla V(y+\sqrt\eta w)\).  Weak integration by parts
under the conditional density gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(W,b_y(W)\mid y)=D_y,\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(b_y(W)\mid y)\preceq
 \frac{\beta\eta}{1-\beta\eta}D_y.
\]
Conditional Poincar\'e applied to linear functions gives
\(\Sigma_y\preceq I\), while the Stein identity
\(\mathbb E[\nabla b_y]=D_y+\operatorname{Cov}(b_y)\) and
\(0\preceq\nabla b_y\preceq\beta\eta I\) give
\(0\preceq D_y\preceq\beta\eta I\).
The second relation follows by applying conditional Poincar\'e to \(b_y\)
and using
\((\nabla b_y)^2\preceq(\beta\eta)\nabla b_y\).
These are standard Brascamp--Lieb/Stein calculations
\citep{chewi2023log}; for a \(C^{1,1}\) potential they follow by
mollification and cutoff.

Differentiating \(\mathsf Tf\) weakly and inserting
\(\mathsf Q\mathsf U\mathsf Pf=L_f+e_f\) yields
\[
 \nabla(I-\mathsf T)f
 =\nabla f-a_f+2D_ya_f+\eta^{-1/2}
   \operatorname{Cov}(e_f,b_y(W)\mid Y_+=y).
\]
Take its inner product with \(\nabla f+a_f\) and average over \(y\).
Using \(a_f=\mathsf T\nabla f\), exact rearrangement gives
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal R_f+4\mathcal D_f
 ={}&\langle\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f,\nabla f+a_f\rangle
 -2\mathbb E\!\left[a_f^\mathrm{T} D_{Y_+}(\nabla f-a_f)\right]\\
 &-\eta^{-1/2}\mathbb E\!\left[
   \operatorname{Cov}(e_f,b_{Y_+}(W)\mid Y_+)^\mathrm{T}(\nabla f+a_f)\right].
\end{align*}
Cauchy--Schwarz, the two conditional covariance bounds above, and the first
inequality control the right-hand side by
\[
 2\lVert\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert\lVert\nabla f\rVert
 +C\sqrt{\beta\eta\,\mathcal R_f\mathcal D_f}
 +C\sqrt{\beta\eta\,\mathcal R_f
                 (\beta\eta\,\mathcal R_f+\mathcal D_f)}.
\]
For sufficiently small \(\beta\eta\), Young's inequality absorbs the last
two terms and proves \cref{persistent:eq:affine-control}.

label: persistent:lem:joint-quarter
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Approximate quarter rotation

title: Proof
body_md:
For fixed reference \(e\), the generator in
\cref{eq:persistent-generator} maps
\(\ell_{a,y}\) to \(m_a\) and maps \(m_a\) to
\(-\ell_{a,y}+k_{a,e}\), where, with
\(r=b_y(w)-b_y(e)\) and
\(Z=p^\mathrm{T} r/\lVertr\rVert\),
\[
 k_{a,e}
 =\mathbb E[a^\mathrm{T} b_y(W)\mid y]-a^\mathrm{T} b_y(e)
  -2a^\mathrm{T} r\,Z^2\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}.
\]
When \(r=0\), only the final term is defined to be zero; the first two
terms are unchanged.
The localized Dynkin formula therefore gives, at \(T=\pi/2\),
\[
 S_T^{y,e}\ell_{a,y}-m_a
 =\int_0^TS_s^{y,e}k_{a,e}\cos s\,\mathrm{d} s,\qquad
 S_T^{y,e}m_a+\ell_{a,y}
 =\int_0^TS_s^{y,e}k_{a,e}\sin s\,\mathrm{d} s.
\]
This is the variation-of-constants identity for the two observable
equations (equivalently, a localized Dynkin formula).  Localization is
legitimate because the harmonic energy in the proof of
\cref{persistent:lem:fixed-invariance} is conserved; dominated convergence
then removes the cutoff.

When \(e\) is an independent conditional draw, elementary Gaussian moments
give
\(\mathbb E k_{a,e}^2=11\operatorname{Var}(a^\mathrm{T} b_y(W)\mid y)\).
The covariance calculation in the proof of
\cref{persistent:lem:affine-control} bounds this variance by
\(L_\eta(1-L_\eta)^{-1}a^\mathrm{T} D_ya\).  Contractivity of \(S_s^{y,e}\)
and Cauchy--Schwarz in time prove the claimed bound.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First let \(f\in\mathcal C_0\).  Apply
\cref{persistent:lem:joint-quarter} conditionally with coefficient
\(2\sqrt\eta\,a_f(y)\), then add the remainder \(e_f\) from
\cref{persistent:lem:affine-control}.  The first two terms on the left of
\cref{persistent:eq:three-side} are bounded by
\(C\{\beta\eta^2\mathcal D_f+\lVerte_f\rVert^2\}\).

For the third term, reflection exchanges \(Y_+\) and \(Y_-\) without
changing momentum.  Since \(\mathsf T\succeq-I/2\),
\(\lVert\mathsf U M_f-M_f\rVert^2\le4\eta\mathcal R_f\).
\Cref{persistent:eq:affine-control} now bounds the sum of all three terms
by
\[
 C\eta\lVert\nabla(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert\lVert\nabla f\rVert.
\]
Equivalently, on \(\mathcal C_0\) we have the pre-spectral estimate
\begin{equation}
 \lVert\boldsymbol{\mathsf E}f\rVert^2
 \le C\eta\lVertD(I-\mathsf T)f\rVert\lVertDf\rVert.
 \label{persistent:eq:pre-spectral-transfer}
\end{equation}

Now take an arbitrary \(f\in\mathcal H_+\).  By
\cref{persistent:lem:closed-gradient-smoothing},
\(f\in\operatorname{Dom}(D)\).  Because \(\mathcal C_0\) is a graph
core, there are \(f_n\in\mathcal C_0\) with \(f_n\to f\) and
\(Df_n\to Df\).  The approximants are not required to lie in
\(\mathcal H_+\).  The graph continuity proved above gives
\[
 \boldsymbol{\mathsf E}f_n\to\boldsymbol{\mathsf E}f,
 \qquad
 D(I-\mathsf T)f_n\to D(I-\mathsf T)f.
\]
Passing to the limit in
\cref{persistent:eq:pre-spectral-transfer} and only then applying the two
sector derivative estimates in
\cref{persistent:lem:outer-geometry} proves
\cref{persistent:eq:three-side}.  Thus no density assertion about
\(\mathcal C_0\cap\mathcal H_+\), and no smoothness preservation by the
spectral projection, is used.

label: persistent:cor:factorized-errors
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Controlled transfer errors

title: Proof
body_md:
\Cref{persistent:eq:three-side}, with \(f\) replaced by
\(\Gamma^{-1}f\), gives
\(\lVertF_jf\rVert^2\le C\lVertf\rVert\lVert\Gamma^2f\rVert\).
Partition the spectrum of \(\Gamma^2\) into dyadic intervals between
\(cg^2\) and \(1\).  On each spectral component \(f_r\),
\(\lVertF_jf_r\rVert^2\le C\langlef_r,\Gamma^2f_r\rangle\).
There are \(O(\ell_g)\) components, so the triangle inequality followed by
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 F_j^*F_j\preceq C\ell_g\Gamma^2.
\]
Since \(\Gamma\) is invertible on the centered subspace, setting
\(B_j=F_j\Gamma^{-1}\) proves
\cref{persistent:eq:factorized-errors}.  The factor order is important;
no commutation between \(B_j\) and \(\Gamma\) is used.
head: environment

label: persistent:prop:ideal-contraction
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Ideal persistent contraction

label: persistent:lem:resolvent
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Unit-circle resolvent bound

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Step 1: isolate the three slow coordinates.}
Fix \(\lvertz\rvert=1\) and solve
\((z-\mathsf K)f=b\).  Write \(f_\perp=\mathsf Qf\).
Let
\(\Pi_{\rm slow}=\mathbf1_{[1/2,1]}(\mathsf T)\), and split the
\(Y\)-only component into
\(x_{\rm slow}=\Pi_{\rm slow}\mathsf Pf\) and
\(x_{\rm fast}=(I-\Pi_{\rm slow})\mathsf Pf\).
In the three-coordinate calculation, every occurrence of
\(\mathsf T,\Gamma,\mathsf V,\mathsf A,F_j\) is restricted to
\(\mathcal H_+=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_{\rm slow})\); equivalently,
\(\mathsf V\) means \(\mathsf V\Pi_{\rm slow}\), and similarly for the
other maps.  The other two tested coordinates are then
\(v=\mathsf V^*f_\perp\) and \(m=\mathsf A^*f_\perp\).

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lp{0.67\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
coordinate & information it measures\\
\midrule
\(x_{\rm slow}\) & the slowly changing component stored in the auxiliary
variable \(Y\)\\
\(v=\mathsf V^*f_\perp\) & conditional variation aligned with the position
signal\\
\(m=\mathsf A^*f_\perp\) & conditional variation aligned with the momentum
signal\\
\(x_{\rm fast}\) & the remaining \(Y\)-modes, controlled directly by the
spectral gap of \(z-\mathsf T\)\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The next identities encode the approximate quarter-rotation in these
coordinates; their error terms are precisely the factorized \(F_j\)'s from
the preceding subsection.  The adjoint identities used below are
\[
 \mathsf V^*\mathsf Su=-\mathsf A^*u+F_1^*\mathsf Ru,\quad
 \mathsf A^*\mathsf Su=\mathsf V^*u-F_2^*\mathsf Ru,\quad
 \mathsf V^*\mathsf U\mathsf Q=-\mathsf T\mathsf V^*,\quad
 \mathsf A^*\mathsf U=\mathsf A^*+F_3^*.
\]
They follow from \cref{persistent:eq:normalized-transfer}, momentum
reversal, and the even/odd momentum parity recorded there.  No
\(x_{\rm fast}\) term is omitted below: spectral orthogonality gives
\(\mathsf V^*\mathsf U\mathsf P x_{\rm fast}=0\), while momentum parity
gives \(\mathsf A^*\mathsf U\mathsf P x_{\rm fast}=0\) and
\(F_3^*\mathsf P x_{\rm fast}=0\).

Projecting the resolvent equation onto these coordinates gives
\begin{align}
 (z-\mathsf T)x_{\rm slow}+k\Gamma m
   &=b_0+k\Gamma r_1,\notag\\
 zv-\Gamma x_{\rm slow}-k\mathsf Tm
   &=b_V-k\mathsf Tr_1,\label{persistent:eq:three-coordinate-system}\\
 zm-kv&=b_A+kr_2,\notag
\end{align}
where \(b_0=\Pi_{\rm slow}\mathsf Pb\),
\(b_V=\mathsf V^*b\), \(b_A=\mathsf A^*b\), and
\[
 r_1=F_1^*\mathsf Rf_\perp,\qquad
 r_2=-F_2^*\mathsf Rf_\perp+F_3^*\mathsf Sf_\perp.
\]
\Cref{persistent:cor:factorized-errors} implies
\[
 \lVert\Gamma^{-1}r_1\rVert+\lVert\Gamma^{-1}r_2\rVert
 \le C\sqrt{\ell_g}\lVertf_\perp\rVert.
\]
This is the only logarithmic loss.  The factorization
\(F_j^*=\Gamma B_j^*\) is used in this order; no commutation is assumed.

\emph{Step 2: invert the three-coordinate system.}
All coefficients on the left of
\cref{persistent:eq:three-coordinate-system} are functions of the single
self-adjoint operator \(\mathsf T\).  At a scalar spectral value
\(t\in[1/2,1)\), put \(\gamma_t=\sqrt{1-t^2}\).  The determinant of the
coefficient matrix is
\[
 d_{t,k}(z)=z^3-tz^2-k^2tz+k^2.
\]
Taking the first row of the adjugate gives the exact operator identity
\begin{align}
 d_{\mathsf T,k}(z)x_{\rm slow}
 ={}&(z^2-k^2\mathsf T)b_0-k^2\Gamma b_V-kz\Gamma b_A\notag\\
 &+kz^2\Gamma r_1-k^2z\Gamma r_2.
 \label{persistent:eq:adjugate-row}
\end{align}
The cancellation that produces the final two terms in this form is what
prevents an extra factor \(g^{-1}\).

We use two elementary scalar estimates.  If
\(\lvertz-t\rvert<\gamma_t/16\), then
\[
 \lvertd_{t,k}(z)\rvert\ge\frac{15}{32}\gamma_t^2,\qquad
 \lvertz^2-k^2t\rvert\le4(\rho+\gamma_t).
\]
For the first, write \(z=e^{2iu}\).  The near condition gives
\(\lvertu\rvert\le\gamma_t/16\), while the real part of
\(e^{-3iu}d_{t,k}(e^{2iu})\) is
\((1+k^2)\{\cos(3u)-t\cos u\}\).
The identity
\(\cos(3u)-t\cos u=(1-t)\cos u-2\sin(2u)\sin u\), together with
\(1-t=\gamma_t^2/(1+t)\), proves the lower bound.  The second estimate
follows from
\(\lvertz^2-k^2t\rvert\le2\lvertz-1\rvert+(1-t)+(1-k^2)\).

On the spectral region
\(\lvertz-t\rvert\ge\gamma_t/16\), the first row of
\cref{persistent:eq:three-coordinate-system} directly controls
\(x_{\rm slow}\).  On its complement, apply the two scalar estimates to
\cref{persistent:eq:adjugate-row}.  The terms involving \(b\) cost at most
\(C(\rho/g^2+g^{-1})\lVertb\rVert\), while
\cref{persistent:eq:factorized-errors} bounds the two error terms as
follows.  If \(E\) denotes this near spectral region, then
\[
 \lVert\mathbf1_Ed_{\mathsf T,k}(z)^{-1}\Gamma F_j^*q\rVert
 =\lVert\mathbf1_Ed_{\mathsf T,k}(z)^{-1}\Gamma^2B_j^*q\rVert
 \le C\sqrt{\ell_g}\lVertq\rVert.
\]
Here the lower bound on \(d_{t,k}\) cancels the two powers of
\(\gamma_t\) supplied by \(\Gamma^2\).  Since
\(\Gamma\succeq cgI\) and
\(\rho\asymp g\sqrt{\ell_g}\), both regions yield
\begin{equation}
 \lVert\mathsf Pf\rVert
 \le C\sqrt{\ell_g}
 \left(\lVertf_\perp\rVert+\frac{\lVertb\rVert}{g}\right).
 \label{persistent:eq:macro-resolvent}
\end{equation}
Here the fast component has not been dropped: on
\([-1/2,1/2)\), \(z-\mathsf T\) has inverse norm at most two, so
\(\lVertx_{\rm fast}\rVert\le2(\lVertb\rVert+\lVertf_\perp\rVert)\).

\emph{Step 3: control everything not tested above.}
\Cref{persistent:eq:dissipation} and
\(\mathsf Kf=zf-b\) imply
\(\rho\lVertf_\perp\rVert^2\le2\lVertf\rVert\lVertb\rVert\).
Combine this with
\cref{persistent:eq:macro-resolvent}, use
\(f=\mathsf Pf+f_\perp\), and apply Young's inequality.  The result is
\[
 \lVertf\rVert\le\frac{C\sqrt{\ell_g}}g\lVertb\rVert.
\]
Thus \(z-\mathsf K\) is bounded below and has closed range.

It is also onto.  Otherwise some nonzero \(u\) would satisfy
\(\mathsf K^*u=\bar z u\).  Because \(\mathsf K\) is a contraction and
\(\lvertz\rvert=1\), equality of norms implies
\(\mathsf K\mathsf K^*u=u\), and hence \(\mathsf Ku=zu\).  This
contradicts the lower bound at \(z\), proving the asserted resolvent
estimate.

label: persistent:lem:resolvent-decay
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:resolvent-decay}
Let \(Q\) be a contraction on a Hilbert space.  If
\(\sup_{\lvertz\rvert=1}\lVert(z-Q)^{-1}\rVert\le M\) with \(M\ge1\), then
\(\lVertQ^n\rVert\le2\exp(-cn/M)\).
head: environment
name: Unit-circle bound implies geometric decay

title: Proof
body_md:
For \(a_j=\sin((j+1)\pi/(N+2))\), apply the resolvent bound to
\(\sum_{j=0}^Na_jz^{-j-1}Q^jf\) and integrate over the unit circle.
Parseval's identity gives
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^Na_j^2\lVertQ^jf\rVert^2
 \le M^2\sum_{j=0}^{N+1}(a_j-a_{j-1})^2\lVertQ^jf\rVert^2,
 \qquad a_{-1}=a_{N+1}=0.
\]
Contractivity and
\(\sum(a_j-a_{j-1})^2
=2\{1-\cos(\pi/(N+2))\}\sum a_j^2\)
imply \(\lVertQ^N\rVert\le\pi M/(N+2)\).  Taking
\(N_0=\lceil2\pi M\rceil\) gives
\(\lVertQ^{N_0}\rVert\le1/2\); writing \(n=qN_0+r\) proves the claim.

name: Implementation theorem

label: persistent:lem:warm-path-transfer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:warm-path-transfer}
Let an exact Markov kernel preserve \(\pi\), and let
\(\nu\ll\pi\) satisfy \(D_2(\nu\Vert\pi)\le\Delta\).  If \(A\) is an
event determined by a Markov path together with all its internal
randomness, then
\[
 \Pr_\nu(A)\le e^{\Delta/2}\Pr_\pi(A)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently, if the stationary one-step probability that an exact and an
approximate transition disagree is at most \(a\), their \(N\)-step laws
started from \(\nu\) can be coupled with disagreement probability at most
\(Ne^{\Delta/2}\sqrt a\).
head: environment
name: Warm path comparison

title: Proof
body_md:
For \(R=\mathrm{d}\nu/\mathrm{d}\pi\), conditional Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\(\mathbb E_\pi[R\Pr(A\mid X_0)]\le\lVertR\rVert_2\Pr_\pi(A)^{1/2}\).
An invariant exact kernel cannot increase \(D_2\).  Apply the same bound
before each exact transition and take a union bound over the first
disagreement.

label: persistent:lem:gaussian-comparison
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:gaussian-comparison}
Let \(\gamma_\delta=\mathcal N(\delta,I_d)\), and set
\(\tau=2+\log(L/m)\).  If
\(\tau L\le c\) and
\(\tau(L^2d+\lVert\delta\rVert^2)\le c\), then
\[
 \left\|\frac{\mathrm{d}\gamma_\delta}{\mathrm{d} q}\right\|_{L^\tau(q)}
 \le e^{C\tau(L^2d+\lVert\delta\rVert^2)},
 \qquad
 \chi^2(\gamma_\delta\Vert q)
 \le C(L^2d+\lVert\delta\rVert^2).
\]
head: environment
name: Shifted-Gaussian comparison

title: Proof
body_md:
Normalize \(r(0)=0\).  Convexity and \(L\)-smoothness give
\(0\le r(z)\le L\lVertz\rVert^2/2\) and
\(\lVert\nabla r(z)\rVert^2\le2Lr(z)\).  The Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality
and the standard entropy argument \citep{chewi2023log} imply, for
\(0\le tL<1\),
\[
 \log\mathbb E_\gamma e^{t(r-\mathbb E_\gamma r)}
 \le\frac{t^2L^2d}{2(1-tL)},\qquad
 \log\mathbb E_\gamma e^{-t(r-\mathbb E_\gamma r)}
 \le\frac{t^2L^2d}{2}.
\]
For completeness, the second inequality is not obtained by simply changing
the sign in the first.  If
\(A_-(t)=\log\mathbb E_\gamma e^{-t(r-\mathbb E_\gamma r)}\), the same entropy
calculation gives
\(tA_-'(t)-A_-(t)\le t^2L\{\mathbb E_\gamma r-A_-'(t)\}\).
Convexity and \(A_-(0)=A_-'(0)=0\) imply \(A_-'(t)\ge0\), so integrating
\((A_-(t)/t)'\le L\mathbb E_\gamma r\le L^2d/2\) proves the displayed
negative-tilt bound.
Applying these bounds to \(\mathrm{d}\gamma/\mathrm{d} q\) gives
\(\log\mathbb E_q(\mathrm{d}\gamma/\mathrm{d} q)^\tau\le C\tau^2L^2d\).
For the shift,
\(\mathrm{d}\gamma_\delta/\mathrm{d}\gamma
=\exp\{\delta^\mathrm{T} z-\lVert\delta\rVert^2/2\}\).
The law \(q\) is one-strongly log-concave, so its linear functionals are
one-subgaussian after centering.  Weak integration by parts gives
\(\mathbb E_qZ=-\mathbb E_q\nabla r(Z)\), while \(\mathbb E_q\lVertZ\rVert^2\le d\); hence
\(\lVert\mathbb E_qZ\rVert\le L\sqrt d\).  Cauchy--Schwarz and Young's inequality
therefore add at most
\(C\tau^2(L^2d+\lVert\delta\rVert^2)\) to the logarithmic moment.  Taking the
\(\tau\)-th root proves the first claim.  Repeating the calculation at
exponent two and using \(e^u-1\le2u\) in the stated smallness regime proves
the \(\chi^2\) bound.  Mollification and cutoff justify the calculation for
\(C^{1,1}\) potentials.

label: persistent:lem:shifted-transfer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:shifted-transfer}
If \(\tau L\lesssim1\) and \(\tau L^2d\lesssim1\), the conditional kernel using
\cref{persistent:eq:shifted-reference} satisfies
\cref{persistent:prop:three-side,persistent:cor:factorized-errors}, with

head: environment
name: Shifted-reference transfer

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(h=\nabla r\), \(\Sigma=\operatorname{Cov}_q(Z)\), and \(D=I-\Sigma\).  For the
reference force \(\mathcal U=h(G+\delta)\), direct expansion of the
Gaussian momentum moments in the proof of
\cref{persistent:lem:joint-quarter} gives
\[
 \mathbb E k_{a,E}^2
 =6\operatorname{Var}_q(a^\mathrm{T} h)+5\operatorname{Var}(a^\mathrm{T}\mathcal U)
  +5\{\mathbb E_q(a^\mathrm{T} h)-\mathbb E(a^\mathrm{T}\mathcal U)\}^2.
\]
The weak integration-by-parts calculation used in
\cref{persistent:lem:affine-control} yields
\(\operatorname{Var}_q(a^\mathrm{T} h)\le CL\,a^\mathrm{T} Da\).

It remains to control the two Gaussian-reference terms.  If
\(H=\nabla^2r\) denotes the weak Hessian, then
\(\mathbb E_qH=D+\operatorname{Cov}_q(h)\preceq C D\).  H\"older's inequality,
\cref{persistent:lem:gaussian-comparison}, and
\(0\preceq H\preceq LI\) give
\(\mathbb E_{\gamma_\delta}[a^\mathrm{T} Ha]\le C a^\mathrm{T} Da\).
Indeed, \(a^\mathrm{T} Ha\le L\lVerta\rVert^2\),
\(\mathbb E_q[a^\mathrm{T} Ha]\ge m\lVerta\rVert^2\), and the choice
\(\tau=2+\log(L/m)\) makes the resulting H\"older ratio universal.
Gaussian Poincar\'e therefore implies
\(\operatorname{Var}_{\gamma_\delta}(a^\mathrm{T} h)\le CL\,a^\mathrm{T} Da\).
The \(\chi^2\) part of
\cref{persistent:lem:gaussian-comparison}, followed by Cauchy--Schwarz
under \(q\), bounds the squared difference of means by the same quantity.
Hence the local quarter-turn estimate holds with the shifted reference.
The affine lifting in \cref{persistent:prop:three-side}, momentum parity,
and the factorization proof are unchanged.

label: persistent:lem:mode-cap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:mode-cap}
Assume \(\beta\eta\le1\).  Gradient descent with step
\((\beta+\eta^{-1})^{-1}\), initialized at \(y\), finds the certificate
used in \cref{persistent:eq:shifted-reference} using at most
\[
 C\left[1+\log_+
 \left(\frac{\sqrt\eta\lVert\nabla V(y)\rVert}{\sqrt d}\right)\right]
\]
oracle queries.  Under the stationary augmented law, stopping after
\[
 J_B=C\left[1+\log(2+\kappa)
       +\log\left(1+\sqrt{B/d}\right)\right]
\]
iterations fails with probability at most \(2e^{-B}\).
The uncapped output is a Borel function of \(y\).
head: environment
name: Mode certificate and deterministic cap

title: Proof
body_md:
The conditional potential has Hessian between
\(\alpha+\eta^{-1}\) and \(\beta+\eta^{-1}\), hence condition number at
most two.  One gradient step therefore reduces the gradient norm by a
universal factor, which gives the pointwise logarithmic bound.

For the stationary tail, let \(x^\star\) be the global minimizer of \(V\)
and write \(Y=X+\sqrt\eta Z\), where
\(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)\).  Strong log-concavity gives
\(\mathbb E\lVertX-x^\star\rVert^2\le d/\alpha\) and Gaussian concentration around that
scale.  Combining it with the Gaussian norm tail and
\(\lVert\nabla V(Y)\rVert\le\beta\lVertY-x^\star\rVert\) gives, outside an event of
probability \(2e^{-B}\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt\eta\lVert\nabla V(Y)\rVert}{\sqrt d}
 \le2\sqrt\kappa\left(1+\sqrt{2B/d}\right).
\]
Substitution into the pointwise bound gives \(J_B\).  Every finite
gradient-descent iterate and the first iterate meeting the certificate are
Borel functions of \(y\).  Returning the complete pre-reflection state on
cap failure therefore defines a total Markov kernel without violating
conditional independence.

label: persistent:lem:capped-clock
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:capped-clock}
Suppose the normalized residual potential \(r\) has
\(L\)-Lipschitz gradient with \(0\le L\le1\), and the normalized reference is
\(G+\delta_y\), where \(G\) is standard
Gaussian, \(y\mapsto\delta_y\) is measurable, and
\(\sup_y\lVert\delta_y\rVert\le L\sqrt d\).  For \(B\ge1\), set
\(\bar\lambda_B=CL(\sqrt{dB}+B)\).
Replacing the event rate by its minimum with \(\bar\lambda_B\) changes one
stationary transition with probability at most
\(C(1+L\sqrt d)e^{-cB}\).  The capped flight is simulated by homogeneous
Poisson thinning and uses at most
\(1+(\pi/2)\bar\lambda_B\) expected oracle queries, including the query at
the reference.
head: environment
name: Clock cap

title: Proof
body_md:
Conditionally on \(Y=y\), the normalized position is one-strongly
log-concave, while \(G\) and the momentum are Gaussian.  Their norm tails,
the bound \(\lVert\nabla r(w)-\nabla r(e)\rVert\le L\lVertw-e\rVert\), and a
one-dimensional Gaussian tail give, uniformly in \(y\),
\[
 \Pr\{\lambda_t>CL(\sqrt{du}+u)\}\le6e^{-u}.
\]
Invariance from \cref{persistent:lem:fixed-invariance} makes the bound valid
at every time.  Integrating the tail over the quarter-period bounds the
expected excess hazard by \(C(1+L\sqrt d)e^{-cB}\).
Using the same Poisson random measure for the exact and capped clocks
couples the paths until the first excess event.  Conditioning on \(Y=y\)
and then integrating proves the claim for the measurable random center.
Ordinary thinning gives the query bound.

label: persistent:prop:rgo-compiler
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{persistent:prop:rgo-compiler}
There is a universal \(K_{\rm rgo}\) such that the following holds.  Given
\(y\), \(0<\delta<1/2\), and a point \(\widehat x_y\) satisfying
\[
 \lVerty-\eta\nabla V(\widehat x_y)-\widehat x_y\rVert
 \le\sqrt{d\eta},
\]
if
\[
 \eta^{-1}\ge K_{\rm rgo}\beta
 \{\sqrt{d\log(1/\delta)}+\log(1/\delta)\},
\]
the first-order rejection sampler of
\citet[Theorems~3.1 and D.1]{chen2026high} returns
\(\widehat q_y\) with
\(\chi^2(q_y\Vert\widehat q_y)\le\delta^2\) and
\(\chi^2(\widehat q_y\Vert q_y)\le\delta^2\), using at most
\(K_{\rm rgo}\) expected oracle queries after construction of the mode
certificate.
head: environment
name: Approximate RGO

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(A_\varepsilon=\Delta+\log(8/\varepsilon)\) and take
\[
 \delta_{\rm rgo}=\frac{\varepsilon}{8(1+N\rho)},\qquad
 B=C\left\{\Delta+\log\frac{8N}{\varepsilon}
                  +\log(2+d+\kappa)\right\}.
\]
The exact comparison chain uses the measurable shifted reference in
\cref{persistent:eq:shifted-reference}, without mode or clock caps, and an
exact refresh.  \Cref{persistent:lem:shifted-transfer} lets us apply
\cref{persistent:prop:ideal-contraction}; the choice of \(N\) makes its
distance from stationarity at most \(\varepsilon/2\).

The implementable algorithm first reflects \(y\).  It then runs the
\(y\)-initialized mode solver for at most \(J_B\) steps.  On failure it
returns the complete pre-reflection state \((x,y,p)\).  On the refresh
branch it invokes \cref{persistent:prop:rgo-compiler} with tolerance
\(\delta_{\rm rgo}\); otherwise it uses the shifted Gaussian reference and
the clock cap in \cref{persistent:lem:capped-clock}.

Couple both chains until their first disagreement.  The complete error
allocation is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{source}&\text{total TV contribution}\\ \hline
\text{ideal mixing}&\varepsilon/2\\
\text{mode-solver cap}&\varepsilon/8\\
\text{event-clock cap}&\varepsilon/8\\
\text{approximate refresh}&N\rho\delta_{\rm rgo}/2\le\varepsilon/16 .
\end{array}
\]
For the mode and clock errors,
\cref{persistent:lem:warm-path-transfer} converts stationary exponential
tails into path probabilities under the warm exact chain.  The RGO error
is uniform in \(y\), so maximal coupling and kernel telescoping apply
directly.  The entries sum to less than \(\varepsilon\), and projection to \(X\)
cannot increase total variation.

We next check the local conditions.  With
\(\tau=2+\log\kappa\) and
\(L=\beta\eta=c/(\sqrt{d\Lambda_\varepsilon}+\Lambda_\varepsilon)\), reducing \(c\)
gives \(\tau L\lesssim1\) and \(\tau L^2d\lesssim1\).
Also \(\log(1/\delta_{\rm rgo})\lesssim\Lambda_\varepsilon\), so the same step
size verifies the gate in \cref{persistent:prop:rgo-compiler}.

The expected number of refresh calls is
\(N\rho\le C\ell_gA_\varepsilon\).  Each iteration uses at most
\[
 C\{J_B+1+L(\sqrt{dB}+B)+\rho K_{\rm rgo}\}
\]
expected oracle queries.  Here \(J_B\) and \(\ell_g\) are logarithmic, and
the definition of \(\eta\) makes \(L(\sqrt{dB}+B)=O(1)\).  Substituting
\(g^2=\alpha\eta\) proves the theorem and hence
\cref{thm:persistent-finite}.

label: persistent:lem:affine-compiler
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{persistent:lem:affine-compiler}
Suppose a conditional potential is
\[
 \Phi_y(x)=R_y(x)+\frac{\omega}{2}\lVertx-y\rVert^2,\qquad
 m\omega I\preceq\nabla^2R_y\preceq L\omega I,\qquad
 0<m\le L\le1.
\]
Let \(x_*(y)\) denote the unique minimizer of \(\Phi_y\), let
\(G\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)\), and fix \(0<\delta<1/2\).
Let \(\tau=2+\log(L/m)\), and assume
\(\tau L\lesssim1\) and \(\tau L^2d\lesssim1\).
If a measurable point \(\widehat x_y\) satisfies
\[
 \lVert\omega(\widehat x_y-y)+\nabla R_y(\widehat x_y)\rVert
 \le\sqrt{d\omega},
\]
then the reference
\[
 E_y=y-\omega^{-1}\nabla R_y(\widehat x_y)+\omega^{-1/2}G
\]
satisfies the shifted-Gaussian comparison, the local quarter-turn forcing
estimate, and the clock estimate with local smoothness \(L\).  The
certificate is found from \(y\) using
\[
 C\left[1+\log_+
 \frac{\lVert\nabla R_y(y)\rVert}{\sqrt{d\omega}}\right]
\]
oracle queries.  The RGO gate becomes
\[
 1\ge K_{\rm rgo}L
 \{\sqrt{d\log(1/\delta)}+\log(1/\delta)\}.
\]
head: environment
name: Affine local compiler

title: Proof
body_md:
In the coordinate \(z=\sqrt\omega(x-x_*(y))\), the residual has Hessian
between \(mI\) and \(LI\).  Strong monotonicity of
\(x\mapsto\omega(x-y)+\nabla R_y(x)\) bounds the normalized Gaussian shift
by \(L\sqrt d/(1+m)\).  Thus
\cref{persistent:lem:gaussian-comparison,persistent:lem:capped-clock}
apply after replacing \(\beta\eta\) by \(L\).
The proof of \cref{persistent:lem:shifted-transfer} up to its local
quarter-turn estimate applies in these normalized coordinates; lifting
that estimate to the global reflected chain requires the separate scaling
calculation in \cref{persistent:sec:alpha-baseline}.
The condition number of \(\Phi_y\) is at most
\((1+L)/(1+m)\le2\), giving the displayed logarithmic mode cost.
Finally, applying \cref{persistent:prop:rgo-compiler} after the affine
change of variables gives exactly the stated RGO gate.

name: Quadratic-baseline refinement

label: lem:warm-removal-truncation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:warm-removal-truncation}
Suppose a routine has a deterministic number of stages and every
random-length operation is one of the following: a geometric trial count
with uniformly positive success probability; a Poisson count with known
mean \(\Lambda\); or a linearly convergent optimization for which
\[
 N(z)\le C\{1+\log(1+H(z)/a)\},\qquad \mathbb E H(Z)^2\le M^2
\]
under the comparison law relevant to that call.  For every \(\xi>0\), all
such operations can be stopped at deterministic limits so that the chance
of any stop is at most \(\xi\).  The limits add only logarithmic factors to
the original work, apart from the already charged Poisson mean \(\Lambda\).
Returning a fixed fallback output after a stop changes the output law by at
most \(\xi\) in total variation.
head: environment
name: Logarithmic work truncation

title: Proof
body_md:
Geometric tails require \(O(\log(1/\xi))\) trials.  A Poisson variable of
mean \(\Lambda\) is at most
\(\Lambda+C\{\sqrt{\Lambda\log(1/\xi)}+\log(1/\xi)\}\) except with
probability \(\xi\).  Finally, Markov's inequality gives
\(H(Z)\le M/\sqrt\xi\) outside an event of probability \(\xi\); because
\(N\) depends logarithmically on \(H\), this increases its limit by only
\(O(\log(1/\xi))\).  Divide \(\xi\) by the deterministic number of
operations and use a union bound.  Coupling the capped and uncapped routines
until the first stop proves the total-variation statement.

label: prop:warm-removal-posteriors
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Finite posterior interfaces

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{Regular interface.}\quad
After rescaling a
potential whose condition number is \(K\),
\citet[Theorem~7.1(ii)]{chen2026smoothed} constructs the output law of an
implementable algorithm and an analysis-only comparison law that are
arbitrarily close in total
variation, with the latter having constant order-two R\'enyi divergence
from the target.  At constant target divergence its query cost is
\(\widetilde O(K^{7/6}d^{1/6}+K)\); the second term is absorbed by the
first for \(K,d\ge1\).  Applying either reflected finalizer from
this paper to the comparison law and the same capped Markov kernel to the
algorithmic output law costs another \(\widetilde O(K^{1/2}d^{1/4})\).  Total-
variation data processing and the triangle inequality give
\cref{eq:warm-removal-regular-posterior}.

\textbf{HB interface.}\quad
First find a point \(z_y\) satisfying the
observable test
\(\lVert\nabla\Phi_y(z_y)\rVert\le m_u/\sqrt{L_u}\), where
\(\Phi_y(x)=V(x)+\lVertx-y\rVert^2/(2u)\).  Strong convexity then gives
\(\sqrt{L_u}\lVertz_y-x_y^*\rVert\le1\), where \(x_y^*\) minimizes
\(\Phi_y\).  The Gaussian
\(G_y=\mathcal N(z_y,(2L_u)^{-1}I_d)\) then obeys
\(D_q(G_y\Vert q_y)=O_q(d\log(\mathrm{e} K_u))\) for every fixed \(q>1\), by the
usual quadratic sandwich and completion of squares.  Applying
\citet[Theorem~3.2(ii)]{chen2026exact} with output order two, initialize
phase space from \(G_y\) tensored with stationary Gaussian momentum.  The
source theorem's initial budget is then
\(d+D_4(G_y\Vert q_y)=\widetilde O(d)\).  Set its R\'enyi tolerance to
\(O(\delta^2)\), project the output to position, and use
\(\operatorname{TV}^2\le D_2/2\).  This gives
\cref{eq:warm-removal-harmonic-posterior}.  Its high-probability query bound
also includes rejected trials.

\textbf{Random centers and work caps.}\quad
It remains to justify localization at the random center \(y\).  The
conditional objective has gradient \(\nabla V(y)\) at \(y\).  For the
regular interface, the observable test
\(\lVert\nabla\Phi_y(z)\rVert\le\sqrt{2m_ud}\) implies
\(\Phi_y(z)-\min\Phi_y\le d\), as required by the imported warmifier; for
the HB interface we use the test in the preceding paragraph.  Accelerated
optimization started at \(y\) reaches either certificate in
\(\widetilde O(\sqrt{K_u})\) queries, with only logarithmic dependence on
\(1+\lVerty-x_*\rVert\).  This cost is absorbed by both displayed bounds.  Under
the law \(\lambda\), the tail needed to cap this search uniformly follows
from \cref{lem:warm-removal-random-centers} below.  On cap failure the
kernel returns a fixed point; the cap probability is included in
\cref{eq:warm-removal-posterior-error}.
The cap depends only on the known parameters
\(\alpha,\beta,d,B,\delta\), not on the unknown law \(\lambda\).

We next verify the work cap rather than inferring it from an expected-query
statement.  The recursive warmifier has a deterministic number of stages.
Its proof controls the second moments of every center passed to its
gradient-descent subroutines, while its pointwise bound for each such solve
is logarithmic in the center gradient; see
\citet[Theorems~6.1(ii) and~6.5, their proofs, and
Lemmas~D.3--D.4]{chen2026smoothed}.  Thus these
solves satisfy the third case of \cref{lem:warm-removal-truncation}.  Its
remaining rejection loops have geometric tails once their observable mode
certificate holds; this is stated for the RGO component in
\citet[Theorems~3.1 and~D.1]{chen2026high}.  The appended reflected
finalizer in the regular interface has only geometric rejection counts and
Poisson event counts.
The exact-ULD/FORS interface already gives a high-probability query bound.
Applying \cref{lem:warm-removal-truncation} makes the displayed work bounds
deterministic up to their logarithmic factors and charges every stop to
\cref{eq:warm-removal-posterior-error}.  Finally, finite optimization iterates,
Gaussian draws, acceptance tests, and capped stopping rules are Borel
functions of \(y\) and the random seed.  Thus \(\widehat P_y\) is a genuine
Markov kernel rather than a pointwise collection of samplers.

label: prop:warm-removal-capped-finalizer
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Capped reflected finalizer

title: Proof
body_md:
The uncapped guarantees are \cref{flux:cor:general-warmness} and
\cref{eq:persistent-general-complexity}.  The implementable algorithms
have a fixed outer horizon.  Their mode solves have logarithmic pointwise
work bounds and warm-path second-moment control, their rejection counts are
geometric, and their event proposal counts are Poisson with the means
already included in their query-complexity bounds.  Hence
\cref{lem:warm-removal-truncation} applies.  For any additional error budget
\(\xi\), each implementation can therefore be replaced by a total Markov
kernel with a deterministic work bound of the same polynomial order and with at most
\(\xi\) additional total-variation error from every \(D_2\)-warm input.
For the flux method the required estimates are in
\cref{flux:prop:finite-compiler,flux:lem:clock-coupling}; for the
persistent method it follows from
\cref{persistent:lem:warm-path-transfer,persistent:lem:mode-cap,persistent:lem:capped-clock}
together with the same elementary Poisson and
geometric tail bounds.  We use this capped version below so that the query bound remains valid even if the algorithmic and comparison paths have
already separated.
The final assertion is the data-processing inequality for a common Markov
