label: lem:warm-removal-hypercontractivity
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Exact proximal warmification

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\pi_u\) be the observation marginal and define
\(A_u^*f(y)=\mathbb E[f(X)\mid Y=y]\), which maps density ratios on \(\pi\) to
density ratios on \(\pi_u\).  Its adjoint is
\(A_ug(x)=\mathbb E[g(Y)\mid X=x]\), and one Gibbs row has density operator
\(S_u=A_uA_u^*\).  Put \(c_u=1+\alpha u\).  The two-measure heat-flow
inequality of \citet[Theorem~1.2]{kook2025zeroth} states that
\(A_u^*:L^{p_0}(\pi)\to L^{p_1}(\pi_u)\) is a contraction whenever
\(p_1-1=c_u(p_0-1)\).  Duality gives the analogous gain for \(A_u\):
\(A_u:L^{p_1}(\pi_u)\to L^{p_2}(\pi)\) is a contraction when
\(p_2-1=c_u(p_1-1)\).  To see the direction of this second relation, the
conjugate-exponent form of the first one is
\(p_0'-1=c_u(p_1'-1)\), where a prime denotes the H\"older conjugate.

Thus the exponent flow through one Gibbs row is
\[
 L^{p_0}(\pi)
 \xrightarrow{\ A_u^*\ }
 L^{p_1}(\pi_u)
 \xrightarrow{\ A_u\ }
 L^{p_2}(\pi),
 \qquad
 p_2-1=c_u^2(p_0-1).
\]
The two excess-exponent gains therefore multiply and prove the first claim.
After iteration it gives
\(\lVertS_{u_1}\cdots S_{u_m}f\rVert_2\le\lVertf\rVert_{1+G_m^{-2}}\).

For \(p=1+G_m^{-2}\), interpolation between \(L^1(\pi)\) and
\(L^2(\pi)\), using \(\lVertf\rVert_1=1\), gives
\(\log\lVertf\rVert_p\le (p-1)D_2(\nu\Vert\pi)/p\).  Since the output
order-two divergence is twice the logarithm of its \(L^2\) density norm,
\cref{eq:warm-removal-d2-conversion} follows.

label: lem:warm-removal-random-centers
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:warm-removal-random-centers}
Let \(\nu_0\) satisfy \(D_2(\nu_0\Vert\pi)\le B\), and run \(m\) exact
proximal updates with step sizes at most \(1/\alpha\).  Then every position law
\(\nu_j\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\nu_j}\lVertX-x_*\rVert^2\le\frac{C(d+B)}\alpha.
\]
Moreover, all observation-dependent mode searches along the path can be
capped so that the probability of any cap failure is at most \(\delta\),
while their query cost changes only by a factor logarithmic in
\(d,\kappa,B,m,1/\delta\).
head: environment
name: Random-center and path accounting

title: Proof
body_md:
Every exact proximal kernel preserves \(\pi\), so data processing gives
\(D_2(\nu_j\Vert\pi)\le B\).  Hence
\(\operatorname{KL}(\nu_j\Vert\pi)\le B\), and the \(T_2\) inequality for an
\(\alpha\)-strongly log-concave law gives
\(W_2^2(\nu_j,\pi)\le2B/\alpha\).  Combining an optimal coupling with
\(\mathbb E_\pi\lVertX-x_*\rVert^2\le d/\alpha\) proves the moment bound.  Since
\(Y=X+\sqrt uG\) and \(u\le1/\alpha\), the same order of control holds for
the observation.

For the tail statement, let \(\mathbb P_{\nu_0}^{(m)}\) be the law of the
entire exact path, including its observations, and let
\(\mathbb P_\pi^{(m)}\) be the law of the same path started at stationarity.
Because their transition kernels agree,
\[
 \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbb P_{\nu_0}^{(m)}}
      {\mathrm{d}\mathbb P_\pi^{(m)}}
 =\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu_0}{\mathrm{d}\pi}(X_0),
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_{\nu_0}^{(m)}(E)
 \le\mathrm{e}^{B/2}\mathbb P_\pi^{(m)}(E)^{1/2}
\]
for every path event \(E\), where the second inequality is
Cauchy--Schwarz.  Under the stationary path, strong log-concavity and the
independent Gaussian observation give exponential tails for
\(\lVertY-x_*\rVert\).  Because the conditional mode solver converges
geometrically and its stopping test is observable, a threshold with
stationary failure probability at most
\(\mathrm{e}^{-B}\delta^2/(4m^2)\) increases its iteration limit only
logarithmically.  A union bound followed by the displayed path inequality
makes the probability of any cap failure at most \(\delta\).  This bound is
for the whole adaptive path, so no independence between successive centers
is used, and its threshold is determined entirely by the displayed problem
parameters.

label: lem:warm-removal-coarse-compiler
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:warm-removal-coarse-compiler}
Let \(\nu_m^\dagger=\nu_0S_u^m\) be the ideal coarse endpoint with \(m\) as in
\cref{eq:warm-removal-row-count}.  Using either posterior interface in
\cref{prop:warm-removal-posteriors}, there is an algorithmic endpoint
\(\widehat\nu_m\) such that
\(\operatorname{TV}(\widehat\nu_m,\nu_m^\dagger)\le\delta\).  Its number of oracle
queries is deterministically bounded, up to logarithmic factors, by
\(mC_{\rm reg}(K_u,d)\) or \(mC_{\rm HB}(K_u,d)\), respectively.

name: Finite approximation of the coarse path

title: Proof
body_md:
The row-wise coupling has the following form as long as the two paths have
not yet disagreed:
\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
 X_{j-1}^\dagger
 &\xrightarrow{\;Y_j^\dagger=X_{j-1}^\dagger+\sqrt uG_j\;}
 &Y_j^\dagger
 &\xrightarrow{\;q_{Y_j^\dagger}\;}
 &X_j^\dagger,\\[0.25em]
 \widehat X_{j-1}
 &\xrightarrow{\;\widehat Y_j=\widehat X_{j-1}+\sqrt uG_j\;}
 &\widehat Y_j
 &\xrightarrow{\;\widehat P_{j,\widehat Y_j}\;}
 &\widehat X_j.
\end{array}
\]
The shared Gaussian \(G_j\) makes
\(Y_j^\dagger=\widehat Y_j\) whenever
\(X_{j-1}^\dagger=\widehat X_{j-1}\).  At that common observation, we use a
maximal coupling of the two conditional draws.

At row \(j\), apply \cref{prop:warm-removal-posteriors} with total error
budget \(\delta/m\); this budget includes the posterior approximation and
all of its mode and work caps.  Couple the exact and approximate
conditional draws maximally whenever the two paths have agreed so far.  To
avoid conditioning on the agreement event, first generate the entire ideal coarse
path and let \(e_j(y)=\operatorname{TV}(\widehat P_{j,y},q_y)\).  The probability
that the first mismatch occurs in row \(j\) is at most
\(\mathbb E[1_{\text{no earlier mismatch}}e_j(Y_j)]\), which is bounded by
the unconditional exact-path average
\(\mathbb E e_j(Y_j)\le\delta/m\).  Summing over the rows gives total mismatch at
most \(\delta\).  The simultaneous choice of all random-center caps is
justified by \cref{lem:warm-removal-random-centers}.

This is ordinary total-variation telescoping; a Hellinger chain rule is not
needed because the requested accuracy affects both posterior interfaces
only logarithmically.  Crucially, every call is work-capped.  Thus the
query bound remains valid after the first coupling disagreement, even
though the later algorithmic centers no longer have the exact center law.
The ideal coarse endpoint \(\nu_m^\dagger\), rather than the algorithmic endpoint,
is the law to which \cref{eq:warm-removal-d2-conversion} is applied.

title: Proof
body_md:
The optimization selects one of the following three coarse-stage
implementations.  The table states the resulting choices; the algebra below
derives them.
\begin{center}
\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\small{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
Regime & Interface & \(r\) & Coarse-stage cost \\
\midrule
\(d\le\kappa^{16/7}\)
& HB & \(r=\kappa\)
& \(\widetilde O(\kappa^{2/3}d^{1/3}\log(\mathrm{e} B))\) \\
\(\kappa^{16/7}<d<\kappa^8\)
& Regular & \(r=d^{1/8}\)
& \(\widetilde O(\kappa d^{3/16}\log(\mathrm{e} B))\) \\
\(d\ge\kappa^8\)
& Regular & \(r=\kappa\)
& \(\widetilde O(\sqrt\kappa d^{1/4}\log(\mathrm{e} B))\) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Fix \(1\le r\le\kappa\), set \(u=r/\beta\), and use the regular posterior
interface.  Multiplying \cref{eq:warm-removal-regular-posterior} by the row
count in \cref{eq:warm-removal-row-count}, and using
\cref{eq:warm-removal-conditional-kappa}, gives the coarse-stage query complexity
\begin{equation*}
 Q_{\rm reg}(r)
 =\widetilde O\!\left(
 \kappa\{r^{-1}+r^{1/6}d^{1/6}+r^{-1/2}d^{1/4}\}
 \log(\mathrm{e} B)\right).
\end{equation*}
The \(r^{-1}\) term records the constant work of each row.

If \(d\le\kappa^8\), the admissible choice \(r=d^{1/8}\) balances the
last two terms and gives
\(\widetilde O(\kappa d^{3/16}\log(\mathrm{e} B))\).  If
\(d\ge\kappa^8\), choose \(r=\kappa\).  The two nonconstant terms are then
\(\kappa^{7/6}d^{1/6}\) and \(\sqrt\kappa d^{1/4}\); the first is no
larger than the second precisely when \(d\ge\kappa^8\).

For the remaining endpoint, again choose \(r=\kappa\), but use the HB
interface in
\cref{eq:warm-removal-harmonic-posterior}.  There are only
\(O(\log(\mathrm{e} B))\) rows and \(K_u=(\kappa+1)/2\), so this route costs
\(\widetilde O(\kappa^{2/3}d^{1/3}\log(\mathrm{e} B))\).  The harmonic and
regular-interface bounds cross at \(d=\kappa^{16/7}\), while the two regular choices
cross at \(d=\kappa^8\).  Selecting the cheapest route gives exactly
\(\widetilde O(\Psi(\kappa,d)\log(\mathrm{e} B))\).

We now close the distributional argument.  Choose the constants in
\cref{eq:warm-removal-row-count} so that
\(D_2(\nu_m^\dagger\Vert\pi)\le1\), and use
\cref{lem:warm-removal-coarse-compiler} with \(\delta=\varepsilon/4\).  Lift both
\(\nu_m^\dagger\) and \(\widehat\nu_m\) through the same Gaussian
augmentation required by the selected finalizer, and append the same
independent Gaussian momentum when needed.  The lifted ideal coarse law has
the same density ratio relative to stationarity, while total-variation
data processing preserves the \(\varepsilon/4\) discrepancy.

Invoke \cref{prop:warm-removal-capped-finalizer} with final-stage convergence
tolerance \(\varepsilon/4\) and work-cap budget \(\varepsilon/4\), and apply the resulting
single kernel to both augmented laws.  Its output from the ideal coarse law is
within \(\varepsilon/2\) of stationarity.  Because applying the same Markov kernel
cannot increase total-variation distance, the two final outputs remain
within \(\varepsilon/4\) of one another.  The triangle inequality therefore puts
the algorithmic output within \(3\varepsilon/4\) of stationarity.  The finalizer's
\(\widetilde O(\sqrt\kappa d^{1/4})\) query cost is bounded by every branch
of \(\Psi\) in its selected regime.  This proves the second term in the
minimum of \cref{eq:warm-removal-distributional-cost}.  Alternatively,
skip the coarse stage and apply the general-budget bound
\cref{eq:warm-removal-finalizer} directly to \(\nu_0\); this proves the
first term.

Finally, every branch of \(\Psi\) is at most
\(\kappa^{6/7}d^{1/4}\).  For the first branch the ratio is
\(\kappa^{-4/21}d^{1/12}\le1\) because
\(d\le\kappa^{16/7}\).  For the second it is
\(\kappa^{1/7}d^{-1/16}\le1\) because
\(d\ge\kappa^{16/7}\), and the third follows from \(\kappa\ge1\).
This proves the claimed envelope.

label: lem:warm-removal-localization
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:warm-removal-localization}
Starting from \(x_0\), accelerated optimization followed by one explicit
Gaussian draw produces a law \(q_0\) such that
\[
 D_2(q_0\Vert\pi)\le1+\frac d2\log(2\kappa)
\]
using \(\widetilde O(Q_{\rm loc})\) oracle queries.
head: environment
name: Observable localization

title: Proof
body_md:
Run accelerated gradient descent until the observable certificate
\(\lVert\nabla V(x_{\rm ref})\rVert\le\alpha/\sqrt\beta\) holds.  The standard
strongly-convex accelerated rate and
\(V(x_0)-V(x_*)\le\beta\lVertx_0-x_*\rVert^2/2\) give the stated
\(Q_{\rm loc}\) bound.  Strong convexity then implies
\(\sqrt\beta\lVertx_{\rm ref}-x_*\rVert\le1\).

Draw \(q_0=\mathcal N(x_{\rm ref},(2\beta)^{-1}I_d)\).  Strong convexity bounds
the target normalizer by
\(Z\le\mathrm{e}^{-V(x_*)}(2\pi/\alpha)^{d/2}\), while smoothness gives
\(V(x)\le V(x_*)+\beta\lVertx-x_*\rVert^2/2\).  Completing the square yields
\[
 \left\|\frac{\mathrm{d} q_0}{\mathrm{d}\pi}\right\|_\infty
 \le\mathrm{e}(2\kappa)^{d/2}.
\]
An \(L^\infty\) density-ratio bound by \(M\) implies
\(D_2\le\log M\), proving the result.

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply \cref{lem:warm-removal-localization}, followed by
\cref{thm:warm-removal-distributional} with
\(B=1+(d/2)\log(2\kappa)\).  Since \(\log(\mathrm{e} B)\) is polylogarithmic in
\(d\) and \(\kappa\), the coarse-wrapper branch costs
\(\widetilde O(\Psi(\kappa,d))\).  Adding the one-time localization cost
proves the first inequality in \cref{eq:warm-removal-cold-cost}; the
envelope proved above gives the second.
